Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so is complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues and within-subject contrasts of high-calorie versus low-calorie foods, and reports participant details; however, the reported analyses are ROI-based (parameter estimates extracted from a priori ROIs) with no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or coordinate tables presented in the full text. Inclusion requires at least one whole-brain, group-level task activation map (voxelwise) or clearly described whole-brain results. Therefore the study must be excluded (E3).

This study investigates maternal neural responses to infant faces and cries (social/parental cues), not drug cues or the natural reward types targeted in the review (e.g., food or sexual cues). It therefore does not satisfy key inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli of the specified types) or I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli). The full text is complete and does report whole-brain voxelwise analyses (satisfying I5), reports whole-brain results in the text/tables (I6), and provides participant/scanner/processing details (I7). Because I3 and I4 are not met, the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study of food (natural reward) cues meets multiple inclusion criteria: it uses visual food stimuli (I3), reports within-participant contrasts (highly desirable>less desirable; food>non-food) (I4), and reports group-level second-level voxelwise statistics with coordinate-level results and SVC-corrected peaks (I5,I6). However, it does not report essential participant age information or explicitly state the primary processing software used (only indirect mention of marsbar), so it fails inclusion criterion I7 requiring relevant info on participant age, sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an fMRI investigation of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-participant contrasts (fattening food > object, non-fattening > object). It reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). However, group-level analyses were conducted using a region-of-interest (14 predefined ROIs) approach with cluster-thresholding within ROIs; the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group task-evoked statistical map. Because the study reports only ROI-based group analyses and no whole-brain group activation map, it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of sexual (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual pornographic stimuli with within-subject pornographic>neutral contrasts and group-level whole-brain analyses (SPM12). Participant age and sex are reported. However, the manuscript does not report MRI scanner field strength (fMRI acquisition section refers to another source: 'See .'), so it fails inclusion criterion I7 requiring relevant reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. All other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met. Because I7 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded per the review rules (any unmet inclusion criterion leads to exclusion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (food vs. non-food and food vs. blurry baseline) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (t-tests and ANOVA) with cluster-corrected thresholds; coordinates and Talairach/BA locations are provided for key effects. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual monetary incentive cues (rings of $ vs #) and reports within-subject contrasts of reward>neutral (natural reward-related cues vs control). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were performed (AFNI 3dLME) with cluster-level correction and reported statistical maps/ROIs. Participant age and sex, cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (FSL, AFNI) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-subject task effects).

Although this is an fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (food) with clearly reported participants, scanner (3T), stimuli, and SPM2 processing, the analyses are reported using an a priori ROI approach with small-volume correction within defined ROIs. The paper does not present unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps; results are confined to ROIs and SVC-corrected clusters. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual nicotine cues and within-subject task conditions (smoke, neutral, rest), the provided full text reports individualized ROI selection and ROI-based neurofeedback analyses (percent signal change within subject-tailored vACC/dmPFC ROIs) and group-level t-tests on these ROIs. The manuscript does not present or describe an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinate table of whole-brain smoke>neutral activation. Therefore it reports only ROI-based results without qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results, meeting exclusion criterion E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with event-related presentation of food vs visually matched non-food images. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food>non-food, whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (FEAT/FSL) with cluster correction and tables/figures of activations, and provides participant age range/sex information, cue type (food), scanner field strength (Philips 3T), and processing software (FSL). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual cues with within-subject contrasts (HC–control, LC–control) and adequate reporting of participants, scanner (3T), and processing (SPM8), the reported analyses and results are presented as ROI-based/small-volume-corrected activations rather than unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps. The manuscript describes a second-level repeated measures ANOVA but applies an a priori ROI analysis (masks and small-volume correction) and reports ROI activations; there is no clear presentation of unmasked whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain corrected results. Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only results) and does not satisfy the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task activation map (I5). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that presented visual food stimuli (also auditory) and analyzed within-subject contrasts (high- vs low-calorie foods and food vs non-food). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 with cluster-correction and reported task-evoked statistical maps/clusters (with thresholds and cluster extent determined by AlphaSim), satisfying whole-brain reporting standards. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural (sexual/social) reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (male/female faces). It reports within-participant contrasts related to reward cues versus control stimuli (anticipation of smiling faces vs dysmorphed control images) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain results for main effects and exploratory whole-brain results with coordinates). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (sexual/face stimuli), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using audio/visual (visual) stimuli and includes within-participant contrasts of smoking cues versus matched non-smoking cues. However, all reported group-level analyses were conducted within an a priori ROI mask (ventral medial PFC, ventral striatum/pallidum, insula, hippocampus, amygdala, and dorsal striatum added retrospectively). The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map at the group level; results are limited to ROI-based inference. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. The study reports within-participant contrasts of food>object (food vs. matched object images) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected permutation tests) as well as ROI analyses. Relevant details are provided: participant age and sex, cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (FSL). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual-cue reward fMRI studies.

This study reports development and behavioral validation of visual cue pictures and an fMRI paradigm but did not acquire or analyze any fMRI data. It reports self-reported VAS craving only and no within-participant fMRI contrast of drug-cue > control, no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate results. Therefore it does not meet the core inclusion requirements for neuroimaging studies (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). It is a methods/behavioral validation paper without original human fMRI results, so it must be excluded from a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs. non-alcohol beverage pictures) in adolescents. It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol>non-alcohol) and conducts both ROI and exploratory whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (3dttest++ with cluster correction), with results described in the text for whole-brain clusters. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue reactivity using visual smoking images and within-subject smoking>nonsmoking contrasts, and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, all reported task analyses focus on ROI-based parameter estimates and targeted ROI/mediation models; the manuscript does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain coordinates/figures of an unmasked task effect. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli, with a within-subject food > nonfood contrast and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported. The manuscript provides participant demographics (age, sex distribution implied), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). Whole-brain statistical maps (F, t, r) and cluster-level correction procedures are described; results are reported across the brain and referenced to anatomical labels, fulfilling acceptable reporting via text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are violated.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts comparing food pictures versus neutral objects. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (RFX ANOVA F-maps and conjunction t-maps) are reported, with thresholding and Talairach coordinates for identified fROIs. Relevant participant information (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and reports participant demographics and scanner/processing details (meets I3 and I7). However, it does not report a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control (no food>neutral or food>non-food contrast); instead contrasts Enhance vs Regulate (both conditions use palatable food images), so I4 is not met. Additionally, group analyses were performed using ROI-based small-volume correction without reporting unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps; thus the study effectively reports only ROI-corrected results, triggering exclusion under E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts of food > scenery. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (t maps, peak coordinates, cluster thresholds), and results are described in text, tables, and figures. Participant age/sex (healthy adult males), cue type (food), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software (fmristat) are provided. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of food cue reactivity using personalized guided-imagery (auditory) scripts rather than visual stimuli. The review’s I3 requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, which is not met. The study does meet several other inclusion criteria (within-subject contrasts of favorite-food cue > neutral, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected maps and coordinates reported, and relevant participant/cue/scanner information), but failure to use visual cues is sufficient to exclude it from this meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cost–benefit decision making using a Cigarette Purchase Task (economic choices about purchasing cigarettes), not a cue-reactivity paradigm presenting visual drug- or reward-related cues. It does not include within-participant contrasts of drug-cue > control-stimuli or natural-reward-cue > control-stimuli. The paper does report group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and provides participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength and processing software, so it meets I5, I6, and I7, but it fails to meet key inclusion criteria I3 and I4. Therefore it must be excluded from this meta-analysis focused on visual cue-reactivity.

The article does not report task-based fMRI cue-reactivity using visual drug or natural-reward cues. The neuroimaging reported is resting-state fMRI and diffusion tensor imaging (structural) in relation to mindfulness training; behavioral measures (craving, smoking) are reported but there are no within-subject contrasts of drug-cue > control-stimuli or whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Thus it fails to meet inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5 and matches exclusion criterion E4 (resting-state/structural analyses without a whole-brain task activation map).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (food) using visual stimuli (food words). It includes within-subject contrasts of food>neutral (food-fneu) at the group level, reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and statistical thresholds, and provides participant demographics (age, sex distribution), cue type (food words), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Results are reported as whole-brain effects and coordinates in the text/tables, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and a within-participant contrast (alcohol > pleasant). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (activation in left caudate and occipital cortex) with coordinates and cluster sizes described in the text and refers to supplemental materials for full acquisition and preprocessing details. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is alcohol, and scanner/acquisition/processing details are indicated to be available in the Supplement. The study therefore satisfies the review’s requirements for an fMRI drug-cue visual stimulus task, a within-subject drug>control contrast, whole-brain results reported in the text/tables, and reporting of participant and methodological details (with additional scanner/software details provided in supplement). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains whole-brain within-subject effects, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food pictures) with within-participant contrasts of food vs non-food stimuli, and group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (random-effects, voxelwise maps) identifying brain regions responsive to food cues. Participant age and sex and cue type are reported; MRI acquisition and preprocessing details are indicated to be provided in the supplementary material, satisfying reporting requirements. The study thus meets the meta-analysis objective (visual reward cue-reactivity) and all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task activation maps, is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of a natural reward (food) using visual cues (milkshake image vs water) and tastes. It reports within-participant contrasts of milkshake cues > control (milkshake picture > water picture) and milkshake taste > tasteless, and conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using FSL with cluster-based correction. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are all reported. Results are presented as whole-brain clusters described in the text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject contrast of high-calorie > low-calorie food images. The methods report fMRI acquisition (3T) and processing (SPM8) and participant age/sex characteristics. Although the primary reported effect is in the hypothalamus using an ROI and small-volume correction, the authors explicitly state they carried out an exploratory whole-brain (voxelwise) analysis (at p<0.05 FWE) and report the outcome (no other regional differences). Thus a group-level whole-brain task analysis was performed and reported in the text. All required information (cue type, scanner field strength, software) is provided and the full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Given these elements, the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual natural reward cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts relevant to cue-reactivity (e.g., healthy-food-choice > healthy-food-reject, and Tasty-Diet (TD) > No-Diet (ND) conditions), conducted at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8). Coordinates and cluster results are reported and scanner parameters (3T), participant age/sex/BMI, cue type (food), and processing software are provided. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity with whole-brain results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (a natural reward). It contains within-subject contrasts of food > nonfood, reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with corrected cluster results and coordinates, and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with a within-participant contrast of palatable food > neutral items. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (FWE-corrected effects, Talairach/MNI coordinates reported), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The paper reports participant age range (adolescents/young adults), mentions sex comparisons, cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3.0T) and processing software (SPM8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of high-calorie vs. non-food images (pre- and post-meal), and presents group-level whole-brain, voxelwise statistical maps with cluster-based correction and Talairach coordinates. Relevant metadata are provided (participant age and sex, cue type = food, scanner field strength = 3.0 T, processing software = BrainVoyager). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (food pictures) vs nonfood control (animals) to assess reward-related cue reactivity in overweight adolescent girls. The study reports within-participant contrasts (food > nonfood) and conducts group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses with cluster-level correction. Key methodological details required by the review are reported: participant age and sex (15–20 y, female), cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3-Tesla Siemens Trio), and processing software (Brain Voyager QX). Full article text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI investigation of response inhibition using abstract visual stimuli (geometric shapes) in methamphetamine-dependent and control participants. It does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity (no drug/food/sexual cues), nor does it include a within-subject contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural-reward cues > control stimuli. Thus it fails inclusion criteria I3 and I4. The full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, and discussion).

This is a human fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of cocaine/paraphernalia). It includes a within-subject contrast of cocaine pictures > neutral objects and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM8 with cluster-level correction, with results described in the text (activation in putamen, insula, occipital cortex) and supplemental figures. Relevant participant information (age range 18–65, men and women), cue type (cocaine), MRI field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an adult fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts of alcohol vs. neutral cues. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t-test of alcohol>neutral, whole-brain regression vs. SCR) with peak coordinates and cluster statistics described. Participant demographics (age used as covariate, sex counts reported), cue type (alcohol), and processing software (SPM) are specified; scanner details are likely in the Supplement (acceptable per inclusion criteria). The study therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue fMRI whole-brain task activation maps and reports necessary methodological details.

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (beer images) in a Go/NoGo task comparing responses to alcohol vs non-alcohol stimuli. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (thresholded whole-brain maps) and presents activation maps for NoGo (beer) trials and between-group contrasts (heavy > light) with whole-brain inference. Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. Individual subject-level contrasts for Go and NoGo conditions were created and entered into second-level analyses, providing the within-participant condition contrasts needed for cue>control comparisons. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues with within-participant food>non-food contrasts and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, the manuscript reports results derived from region-of-interest (ROI) percent signal-change extractions and does not present or describe group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, coordinates, or cluster tables in the provided full text. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results).

Although this is an empirical fMRI study in cocaine-dependent individuals that includes cue exposure for behavioral craving measures, the MRI analyses do not report a within-participant visual cue-reactivity contrast (drug cues > control stimuli). The reported whole-brain voxelwise maps are TMS-evoked BOLD responses and pre/post cTBS (real vs sham) effects, not task-based cue-reactivity to visual drug cues. Therefore criteria I3 and I4 (fMRI of visual cue-reactivity and a within-subject cue>control contrast) are not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present) but no qualifying cue-reactivity fMRI maps are described. Exclusion from the meta-analysis is warranted.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (viewing food > viewing non-food; distraction food > distraction non-food). Analyses are group-level whole-brain voxelwise using SPM8 with reported cluster coordinates and thresholding (FWE cluster-corrected), and the paper reports participant sex/age, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures/videos and written visual cues). It includes within-subject contrasts CUE SEM > CUE NEUTRAL and SEM > NEUTRAL, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected clusters and coordinates), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of monetary reward anticipation using the Monetary Incentive Delay task (visual cues for £5, £1, £0). Although it includes within-participant reward>neutral contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates, and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM8), it does not assess drug-related cues or natural reward-related cues (e.g., food, sexual) as defined by the review objective. Monetary reward cues do not meet the meta-analysis’s specified domain of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3.

This is an empirical fMRI study employing visual alcohol cues (alcohol-related images) and neutral images in an alcohol cue reactivity (ACR) task. It reports within-subject alcohol>neutral contrasts (GLM, one-sample t-tests) and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation results (alcohol > neutral) with voxelwise and cluster-level correction. Participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio) and detailed acquisition parameters are reported; preprocessing is referenced and reported in Supplementary Methods (fulfilling reporting requirements). The study therefore satisfies all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cue-induced desire for Internet video game play using visual stimuli. It includes a within-subject contrast (video-game cue > neutral control), reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects results with coordinates and cluster statistics (FDR-corrected), and provides participant age/sex information, scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). Although the cue type is Internet video game (a behavioral/non-drug reward), the review objective includes drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity; gaming can be considered a non-drug reward cue within that scope. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the inclusion criteria for whole-brain task-evoked cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

The reported fMRI results in this full text focus on emotional face processing (faces vs shapes) and oxytocin modulation, not on drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity contrasts. Although an alcohol cue-reactivity task was performed, its results are reported in a parent study and are not presented here. Therefore the paper does not provide a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast nor a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map of drug or natural reward cue-reactivity required for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking > control). However, the voxelwise second-level analyses were conducted within anatomically defined ROI masks (Harvard-Oxford atlases) and results are presented as ROI-based activations/deactivations. There is no evidence in the full text that an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map was performed or reported. Therefore the study reports only ROI-restricted task results and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). The full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in heavy drinkers using visual cues (images) of alcohol and food (natural reward). The AFID task included within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs neutral and alcohol vs food) and the manuscript reports group-level, voxel-wise whole-brain analyses (linear mixed-effects voxel-wise analyses across the entire brain) with thresholding and cluster correction. Relevant methodological details are reported (participant age/sex information, cue types: alcohol and food, MRI scanner field strength 3T, and processing software AFNI). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided content appears complete for screening. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The fMRI task used an alcohol taste-cue paradigm and the primary contrast analyzed was Alcohol (taste) > Water (taste). Although short visual word prompts (“Alcohol”/“Water”) preceded taste delivery, the neural contrast of interest is sensory (taste) cue delivery rather than a visual cue-reactivity contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant Alcohol>Water contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain task analyses reported), I6 (whole-brain results/descriptions/supplementary material acceptable), and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, scanner/processing details reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Therefore the study should be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts of cocaine>neutral cues, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected and cluster-level thresholds) and presents coordinates/figures/tables. Participant demographics (n=23, sex distribution), cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be included.

This article is a non-empirical review/perspective summarizing a series of ERP and fMRI studies rather than reporting original human fMRI data. The full text does not present new group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or specific drug>control or reward>control contrasts suitable for meta-analysis. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I3–I7 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7.

This is an empirical 1.5T fMRI study using visual cocaine-cue videotapes. It includes within-subject contrasts (tape viewing vs baseline; pre- vs post-onset of craving) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (voxelwise t-maps, randomization procedure, figures/tables). Participant age and sex, cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (1.5-T), and processing software (SPM96) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes task activation maps, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study is excluded because it does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., alcohol>food or alcohol>neutral) at the group whole-brain level, so it fails inclusion criterion I4. It is an fMRI study using visual alcohol and food cues (I3 met), includes whole-brain group-level maps for regulation contrasts and a parametric craving analysis (I5 met), reports results/coordinates in the text/tables (I6 met), and provides participant/cue/scanner/software details (I7 met). However, the primary reported fMRI contrasts are regulation-focused (LATER>NOW, REAPPRAISE>LOOK) and a parametric modulation by craving; a parametric craving regressor does not substitute for an explicit cues>control within-subject contrast required by I4. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of heroin-maintained patients using visual drug-related cues (24 heroin-related photographs) versus neutral images. It reports within-participant contrasts (BOLD_drugcues > BOLD_neutral) and group-level voxelwise (whole-brain) analyses with clusterwise FWE-corrected results (reported in text/tables/figures). Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is heroin, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM8, VBM8) are described. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in children. It reports a within-subject contrast of food > non-food cues, and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME1, cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<.05) with results presented in figures and tables. Relevant metadata are provided (participant age/sex, cue type=food, 3T scanner, processing software=FSL). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full-text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study of smokers with schizophrenia vs control smokers used visual smoking cues and neutral images and reports within-subject Smoking>Neutral contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FSL FLAME, cluster-corrected results reported and tabulated/figured). Relevant participant information (age range, sex/gender matching), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity fMRI studies (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cocaine cues and neutral controls with within-subject cocaine>neutral contrasts. Group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses were performed and reported (one-sample t-test across participants, independent-samples t-test, and regression analyses) using SPM8 with cluster-level correction. Participant characteristics (sex reported; age likely provided in Table 1 referenced), cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (Siemens 3.0T), and processing software (SPM8) are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues and reports within-subject contrasts (Alcohol > Control). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level GLMs were conducted and corrected, and results are reported with cluster-level statistics and MNI coordinates. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T GE) and processing software (SPM12). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, references).

The study is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol (within-participant alcohol>juice contrast) and reports group-level voxelwise results, scanner/processing details, and participant age/sex. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, and I7. However it does NOT meet I3 because the cue modality is gustatory (taste: alcohol vs juice) rather than visual stimuli required by the review objective. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are triggered. As a result, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis focused specifically on visual cue-reactivity.

This study contains an fMRI experiment using visual alcohol cues (alcohol vs neutral pictures) in a within-subject crossover design, satisfying the drug-cue visual stimulus requirement. The authors report within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral) for OXT and placebo conditions and present group-level whole-brain task-activation results (cluster-based, FWE-corrected results reported; Figure 5 and Table 1), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are reported in figures/tables and main text. Participant age and sex (male, mean age reported) and cue type (alcohol images) are reported; scanner details and processing software are referenced as provided in Supplementary Information (acceptable per protocol since supplementary material may contain methodological details). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary methods are referenced but missing here — however missing supplements are acceptable, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study does not meet the core review requirement of assessing visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward stimuli. Although it includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI results and reports necessary methodological details, the fMRI paradigm is a monetary incentive delay (reward anticipation) task (anticipation of monetary reward > verbal feedback) rather than a visual drug- or natural reward-cue reactivity task (e.g., pictorial alcohol, food, sexual cues). Therefore inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study using visual video cues (cocaine, gambling, sad) that elicited cue-related responses. Within-subject contrasts comparing video epochs to baseline (V1>B1, V2>B2) and direct cocaine>sad/gambling comparisons are reported. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (3×2×3 ANOVA) with FWE correction and reported in tables/figures and text. Participant age and sex are provided, cue types specified (cocaine, gambling), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio) and processing software (SPM5, AFNI, BioImage Suite) are reported. Full article core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a human fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (images), with within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral) reported. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8/SPM12) and reports whole-brain results with tables/figures and ROI follow-ups; scanner field strength (3T), processing software, participant sex and age range, and cue type (alcohol visual cues) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, fMRI task, acquisition, preprocessing, statistical analyses), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it is not an fMRI cue-reactivity task: it uses PET ([18F]fallypride) to measure dopamine release during cocaine cue exposure and reports ROI-based PET binding analyses rather than whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI activation maps. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli was performed—cue vs neutral). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (not a functional MRI study), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported), I6 (no whole-brain results reported via coordinates/figures for voxelwise fMRI activation), I7 (required fMRI details such as MRI scanner field strength and fMRI processing software are not reported; modality is PET). Full text appears complete for decision-making (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual stimuli (alcohol and cannabis marketing video clips) to probe cue-reactivity. It includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol marketing > neutral and cannabis marketing > neutral) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLM whole-brain results and cluster tables/figures), along with ROI analyses. Relevant methodological details are reported: participant age and sex, cue types (alcohol, cannabis), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effects, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study uses visual smoking cues (I3) and reports within-subject contrasts of smoke>rest (I4). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3 T) and processing software (SPM/TBV) are reported (I7). However, the paper presents only ROI-based analyses (individualized ACC/mPFC ROIs and PSC extraction) and does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or coordinate table for a smoke>control contrast. Thus it fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based neurofeedback/region-extraction results rather than a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) cue-reactivity map. Exclusion criterion E3 applies. Inclusion criterion I3 is met: this is an fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-related reactivity using visual stimuli. However, the study does not report a within-participant drug-cue > control-stimuli contrast at the whole-brain level (I4 not met), does not provide group-level whole-brain task activation maps or coordinates/tables of whole-brain results (I5/I6 not met), and does not clearly report required participant demographic details in the provided text (I7 not met). The full text appears complete. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results and must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli of the types targeted by the meta-analysis. The task used visual shapes predicting monetary gains/losses (monetary incentive delay) rather than drug cues (e.g., nicotine paraphernalia) or natural reward cues such as food or sexual stimuli. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrasts Reward Cue–Neutral Cue and Loss Cue–Neutral Cue), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type described, MRI field strength and processing software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded for failure to meet I3 (cue-type mismatch). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (meets I3), includes within-subject contrasts of alcoholic vs. non-alcoholic beverages (meets I4), and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and software (meets I7). However, the second-level/group analyses were spatially restricted to an anatomically defined mesocorticolimbic mask rather than an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group map. Therefore the study does not provide an unmasked whole-brain task-evoked group-level statistical map (fails I5) and thus does not satisfy the whole-brain reporting requirements (I6 not met). Exclusion criterion E5 applies: group-level results are reported only within a mask and no unmasked whole-brain task effect is provided. Conclusion: EXCLUDE (E5).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity that includes visual cue conditions (grayscaled images) and within-participant contrasts (e.g., visual smoking vs visual control (VS–VC) and haptic contrasts). Group-level whole-brain random-effects GLMs/ANOVAs and whole-brain ANCOVAs are reported with cluster correction and coordinate tables/figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without whole-brain task maps, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References). Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual-stimulus fMRI cue-reactivity.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: cue presentation modality is auditory personalized imagery scripts (audiotaped scripts eliciting mental imagery), not visual stimuli. Met inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrast: favorite-food vs neutral-relaxing), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction), I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported in tables/figures/text), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type (food), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli in treatment-seeking smokers. It uses a within-subject CUE>neutral contrast (abstinence vs. satiety) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL FLAME1) with corrected statistical maps and figures/tables. Key methodological details required by the review are reported (participant age and sex, cue type: nicotine, 3T Siemens Prisma scanner, processing software: FSL). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual alcohol cues and a combined stop-signal alcohol-cue task. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing alcohol versus control picture trials (CRAlcohol-CRControl) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (family-wise error corrected) with tables/figures. Participant age and sex are reported; cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3.0T Siemens Trio), and processing software (SPM8) are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. The paper reports within-participant task contrasts relevant to cue-reactivity (e.g., ADMIT_TASTY>ADMIT_NOT_TASTY and REGULATE_TASTY>ADMIT_TASTY), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses (voxelwise P<0.001, cluster-level FWE correction). Results are reported in figures and tables of coordinates. Participant information (sex: females; ages reported in Table 1), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Hence the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual natural reward cue-reactivity.

The full text reports an original fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) with within-subject contrast food > nonfood. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (multiple regression and contrasts) with cluster-level correction and coordinates/figures provided. Methods report participant age and sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12). The manuscript contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it's empirical human fMRI data). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

Exclusion reason: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (BOLD fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual [audiovisual] stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of cocaine cues > neutral control). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map is reported in this paper — analyses focus on ROIs/single-slice vermis measures), and I7 (processing software for MRI preprocessing/analysis is not clearly reported). Full text appears complete.

The full text is complete and the study reports a within-subject alcohol>water (control) contrast with whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise results and provides participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, the cue modality is gustatory (alcohol taste delivered in the scanner) rather than visual stimuli, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) required by the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I3. Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis focused specifically on visual cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cocaine-related film stimuli in experienced cocaine users and controls. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing cocaine-film responses to nature (neutral) and sex (natural reward) films in cocaine users, and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation maps (one-sample and two-sample t tests with voxelwise thresholds and cluster criteria). Methods report participant age and sex breakdown, cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (AFNI). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol pictures (heavy drinking participants). The report includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > rest (alcohol cues>control) and group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain results reported for the reward localizer and for clusters during neurofeedback), plus ROI analyses. Relevant sample characteristics (age mean 24.11, sex distribution 29M/9F), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

Full text provided is incomplete (only abstract/metadata). The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using alcohol videos (I3) and reports a within-participant alcohol vs neutral contrast (I4), but the abstract states the simple alcohol>neutral contrast was not significant and the reported results focus on psychophysiological interaction (seed-based connectivity) analyses. There is no clear report of a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map (I5 not confirmed), and key reporting details (participant age/sex, scanner field strength, processing software) cannot be verified from the available content (I7 not confirmed). This meets exclusion criterion E4 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without accompanying whole-brain task activation). Full text incomplete flag set because core article content (methods/results/discussion) is not present for verification.

Full text is incomplete: the provided content is an error message indicating the article could not load, so core article sections (methods, results) are unavailable. I cannot confirm this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli. Title suggests a pharmacologic clinical trial on varenicline and bupropion SR effects on craving, not necessarily an fMRI visual-cue task. Therefore none of the required inclusion criteria (I3-I7) can be verified. No exclusion criteria from the list can be confidently applied based on the truncated content. Excluding on the basis of incomplete full text so the study cannot be assessed for eligibility.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using audiovisual visual stimuli, with within-participant contrasts (smoking cues > nonsmoking cues) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported (coordinates, SPM5). However, the provided full text does not explicitly report the MRI scanner field strength, which is required by inclusion criterion I7 (the manuscript references imaging acquisition methods in prior publications/eAppendix but does not state scanner field strength in the main text provided). Therefore not all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I7 missing), so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject cue>baseline contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (coordinates/figures). However, the manuscript does not report the image processing software package (e.g., SPM, FSL, AFNI) used, which means inclusion criterion I7 (reporting of processing software) is not met. All other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet I7.

This is an fMRI study using visual cannabis cues with a within-participant contrast (cannabis > neutral) and reports participant age/sex, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). However, all reported activation analyses are ROI-based (mean percent signal change in predefined ROIs and ROI-constrained FLAME analyses). The manuscript does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain results outside ROI masks. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain analysis) and I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears to be only the abstract; core methods/results details are missing. The study is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards), so I3 is met. However the abstract does not report any within-participant contrast of food cues > control stimuli (no mention of neutral/control images or a cues>control contrast), so I4 is not satisfied based on available text. It is unclear whether whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed or whether results are ROI-only; I5 cannot be confirmed. Required reporting details (MRI field strength and processing software) are not provided, so I7 is not met. Because the full text is incomplete and multiple inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis at this stage.

The study used an fMRI monetary incentive delay task with monetary cues (gain/loss) rather than drug-related or the natural reward cue types specified by the review (nicotine, alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, heroin, food, sexual). Therefore it does not meet the core inclusion criterion I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (contrast of drug cues > control or natural reward-related cues > control). The study does meet other methodological requirements: it reports group-level whole-brain analyses and voxelwise contrasts (I5), allows whole-brain results reporting in supplementary/tables/figures (I6), and reports participant/sample and processing details including cue type, scanner/processing software (SPM8) (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest analyses and explicitly states “A voxelwise approach was not completed,” indicating no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map was produced. This meets exclusion criterion E3. The study does meet I3 (an fMRI cue–reactivity study using visual cannabis cues) and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength (4T), and processing software (AFNI)). However it does not meet I5 (no whole-brain voxelwise results) and does not provide an explicit within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast as required by I4; I6 is not applicable in absence of whole-brain results. Full text appears complete.

Full text reports an fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol (drinking) and smoking using visual cues with within-participant contrasts (drinking cues > neutral) and provides participant, cue, scanner (3T) and processing (SPM12) details. However, the paper performed and reports region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (VS and MPFC) using extracted ROI timecourses and statistical tests on ROI values; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, coordinates, or voxelwise results are reported in the main text or supplements provided. Therefore Exclusion E3 applies (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcohol-related images) and neutral control images, with within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral). Group-level whole-brain analyses are reported (one-sample t-test and multiple regression with AlphaSim/FWE correction), and results are presented in tables/figures. Relevant participant information (sex distribution, age inclusion range), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T Siemens), and processing software (SPM v5/SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant whole-brain task activation map, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because inclusion criterion I7 is not satisfied: the full text does not report the MRI scanner field strength (e.g., 1.5T or 3T), while I7 requires reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. The study does satisfy I3 (fMRI with visual cigarette and pleasant cues), I4 (within-subject contrasts: cigarette-related and pleasant > neutral), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM with voxelwise thresholding and FDR correction), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/tables of coordinates). No exclusion criteria applied (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it is not an fMRI study and did not use visual cue stimuli: it used [15O]H2O PET imaging and script-guided (auditory) mental imagery. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast of cocaine cues > control stimuli), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported using SPM), I6 (results reported in figures/tables/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (functional MRI with visual stimuli — study used PET and auditory imagery), I7 (requires reporting MRI scanner field strength — not applicable/not reported because this is PET). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Given these mismatches with core modality and stimulus type, the study cannot be included in a meta-analysis limited to fMRI studies using visual cues.

This is an fMRI study of cocaine (drug) and pleasant (natural reward-related) visual cues with within-participant contrasts (CSD+ vs CS−) indexing drug-cue vs neutral control responses. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (see Tables S1–S2 and Figures S3–S4 in the Supplement) in addition to ROI results, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement; whole-brain results are described in the text and supplementary materials. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (4T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study investigates monetary (non-drug) reward anticipation in alcohol-dependent participants using a reaction-time monetary-reward paradigm, not visual drug cues or natural reward-related cues of the types specified by the review (e.g., alcohol cues, food, sexual stimuli). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3. It does meet other inclusion criteria: a within-participant contrast (monetary reward > verbal feedback) (I4), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates (I5/I6), and provides participant demographics, cue description, scanner field strength and processing software (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it reports ROI-based regional analyses without reporting a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map (exclusion E3). It does meet I3 (BOLD fMRI assessing cocaine cue reactivity using visual/audiovisual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of cocaine cues vs neutral segments). However, it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise group results (I5 not met) and does not explicitly report the processing software used (I7 not met). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related vs neutral images). It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) at the group level, with whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses and cluster-corrected maps/tables of peak coordinates. The paper provides participant age and sex (women, mean age reported), cue type (nicotine/smoking images), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, and is empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol stimuli with a within-subject contrast (alcohol > neutral) at first level and group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported (e.g., whole-group alcohol>neutral results, Table S3, Figures). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8/SPM12, AFNI 3DClustSim) are described. Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (not ROI-only), and although it includes seed-based PPI analyses, it also reports whole-brain task-evoked activation, so E3–E5 do not apply; it is empirical human fMRI data (E6 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues versus neutral stimuli in participants on methadone maintenance. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (heroin-related > neutral), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (t-maps and tables of significant coordinates, p<.0001, cluster-level correction), and provides necessary methodological details (participant age and sex, cue type: heroin, scanner field strength: 3T, processing software: SPM5). Full article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual/audio-visual smoking stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking cue > nonsmoking cue) and group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM2 (random effects), with whole-brain statistical maps and coordinates reported in tables/figures. Participant demographics (age range and sex distribution), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM2) are provided. The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3–I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI investigation of monetary (natural) reward cues using visual trial cues and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (meets I3, I5, I6, I7). However, it does not report a within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control (neutral) stimuli or an equivalent unmasked reward>control contrast — cue conditions compare effort levels (low/high/unknown) and success/failure rather than reward cues versus a neutral control stimulus. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Excluded because I4 (within-participant reward>control contrast) is not satisfied, despite meeting I3, I5, I6, I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts smoke > control and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (RFX ANOVA and RFX ANCOVAs) with results corrected for multiple comparisons and presented in tables/figures. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager) are provided. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using visual audiovisual heroin-related cues in abstinent heroin-dependent patients. It reports within-subject contrasts of heroin versus neutral stimuli (drug cues > control), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (session × condition repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster-corrected statistical maps and reported peak coordinates and cluster sizes. Methods report participant age and sex, cue type (heroin), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task activation maps, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (neutral geometric shapes conditioned to alcohol). It reports a within-subject contrast [CS+ > CS−] comparing alcohol-paired vs. saline-paired cues. Analyses are whole-brain, random-effects SPM models with cluster-level FWE correction and reported peak coordinates and tables/figures. Methods report participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Skyra), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-subject whole-brain task activation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete — only references and bibliographic metadata are provided. Although the title suggests an fMRI study of cue-induced smoking craving in virtual environments, the core article content (methods, results, participant information, analyses) is missing, so I cannot verify the required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none (I3-I7 cannot be confirmed). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I3 (cannot confirm fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli from methods), I4 (no evidence of within-participant drug-cues>control contrast), I5/I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or tabulated coordinates are provided), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type details, MRI field strength, and processing software not reported). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 can be assessed because analyses are not described. Per screening rules, set fulltext_incomplete=true and exclude pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (drug words) in cocaine-dependent participants and matched controls. It reports within-participant drug>neutral contrasts, and group-level voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses with coordinates and cluster-corrected results (Table 2, figures). Participant demographics (age/sex matching referenced in Table 1), cue type (cocaine drug words), scanner field strength (4T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task contrasts and whole-brain task activation maps). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided; supplemental material is referenced but not required. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI task study using visual cues (cocaine, sexual, aversive, neutral) with within-participant contrasts (cocaine > neutral) at the first level. The paper reports group-level analyses and explicitly states cluster-corrected whole-brain results (Table 2 and text) in addition to ROI analyses. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (SPM8, FSL, AFNI) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with a within-subject contrast (food > control pictures) and randomized crossover nicotine/placebo sessions. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster- and FWE-corrected results, exploratory whole-brain thresholds, tables/figures) and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is a resting-state fMRI graph-theory study of intrinsic functional connectivity in smokers, not a task-based cue-reactivity experiment. It does not present any drug- or natural-reward visual cue exposures, nor any within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli, and there are no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps reported. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criterion I7 is satisfied (participant age/sex, substance studied = nicotine, scanner field strength, and processing software are reported). Inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), and I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map) are not met. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (smoking images) in a within-subjects design. The authors report within-participant contrasts of smoking versus control cues and perform whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA) with FDR correction for the ventral striatum and additional whole-brain results reported at p<0.001 uncorrected. Relevant methodological and sample details are provided (participant age and sex, cue type: nicotine/smoking, scanner field strength: 3T, processing software: SPM2). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (personal and standard smoking vs nonsmoking images). It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking>nonsmoking cues, and includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected whole-brain results described and reported in figures/tables). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures). It reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral), conducts and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (linear mixed-effects 3dLME) with cluster results and coordinates in tables/figures, and provides scanner field strength (3.0T), processing software (AFNI), and participant age/sex. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

This article reports an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in treatment-seeking smokers. The paper includes within-subject contrasts comparing smoking-related cues > neutral control cues at both individual and group levels, and reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses using mixed-effects (FLAME) with cluster thresholding; results are described in text, tables, and figures. Relevant participant info (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).
