This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (IAPS) to assess neural reactivity to nondrug emotional/natural-reward-related cues in cocaine-dependent participants and controls. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (positive>neutral and negative>neutral) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM8 with voxelwise results and cluster correction. Key participant details (age, sex), cue type (positive/negative emotional/natural cues), scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task activation maps). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (video cues) with within-subject contrasts (heroin vs neutral) computed per subject and voxelwise group-level, whole-brain factorial analyses reported (cluster-corrected maps and coordinate tables). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (AFNI). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper presents an empirical fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (photographs) in human participants. It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking > neutral images, using a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects ANCOVA with cluster correction, and reports cluster coordinates and volumes. Participant age and sex (women, mean age reported), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are described. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3–I7). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study with visual alcohol cues), I4 (within-participant contrast alcohol cues > neutral/control), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses reported with cluster/voxel thresholds), I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 — the paper reports participant age and sex, cue type, and processing software (AFNI), but does not report the MRI scanner field strength, so the required set of details in I7 is incomplete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because all inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I7 is not met, the study is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of methamphetamine cue-reactivity using visual pictorial stimuli with a within-subjects Methamphetamine Cue>Control Cue contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported (cluster-corrected Z-statistic maps and supplementary tables/figures), and required methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software FSL). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are referenced but not required for inclusion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcohol vs. non-alcohol beverage images) with a within-subject contrast (alcohol > non-alcohol). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain ANOVA, cluster-corrected maps; Table 3 and Figure 2 report coordinates/regions). Methods report participant ages/sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T Allegra), and processing software (SPM5 and AFNI). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes whole-brain task activation maps, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

The study is an fMRI experiment using visual smoking cues (videos) with a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (figures/tables) and processing software (FSL). Participant age and cue type are reported. However, the provided full text does not report participant sex distribution or the MRI scanner field strength, which are required per I7. All other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I7.

This is an fMRI study of visual drug-related cue reactivity (subliminal cannabis cues) with within-subject contrasts (cannabis>neutral) at the group level. Although primary ROI-based inference was used, the paper explicitly reports whole-brain analyses (see Online Resource 2) and tables/figures describing voxelwise results, satisfying the requirement for a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map. The manuscript reports participant sex and other demographics, cue types (cannabis, sexual, aversive), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli; it reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol cue > neutral; stress > neutral) and whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level analyses with FWE cluster correction using AFNI/BioImageSuite. Participant demographics (age range, sex), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T Siemens), and processing software are reported. Whole-brain results are presented in text, figures, and supplemental tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. All inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The full text describes an empirical fMRI study using visual cue videos (smoking vs food) in human smokers, reporting within-subject contrasts (Smoking>Food and Smoking>Baseline). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FLAME/cluster correction) and whole-brain results are reported with coordinate tables and figures. Participant age and sex distribution, cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T Trio), and processing software (FMRIB/FSL tools: FILM, FLIRT, FLAME, BET) are all reported. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3–I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it used individualized script-driven imagery (auditory/imagery) to elicit stress and drug-cue responses rather than visual cue stimuli required by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts: drug-cue vs. neutral and stress vs. neutral), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with family-wise error correction), I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/supplement), and I7 (reported participant age and sex, cue type [cocaine/alcohol], 3T scanner field strength, and processing software AFNI). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues in abstinent alcohol-dependent participants. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol-associated > control stimuli) and second-level, voxelwise random-effects group analyses using SPM99. Results are reported as tables/figures with coordinates and clear descriptions. Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (SPM99) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol using visual stimulus blocks and reports within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts (meets I3 and I4). Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported (meets I7). However, the imaging results are reported only as region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (predefined OFC, VS, mPFC) and no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or unmasked whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates are provided. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only report). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete for core content (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (picture-perception task). It reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs control pictures) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (one-sample t-test; Table 2 and Fig.2; FWE-corrected). Methods report participant ages and sex counts, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is an empirical fMRI study but does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (reports whole-brain, task-evoked statistical maps for the working memory task) and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (not an fMRI study of drug/natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward cues > control stimuli), I7 (no reporting of cue type as required for cue-reactivity studies). Exclusion IDs met: none (E3, E4, E5, E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is ineligible for the meta-analysis focused on visual cue-reactivity contrasts and is excluded.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). The authors computed within-subject contrasts (alcohol > soft drink) at the single-subject and second-level group analyses, and report group-level voxelwise t-tests. Whole-brain exploratory analyses are reported in the online supplement (Table S1/S2 and figures), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement despite ROI small-volume corrections for primary hypotheses. The paper reports participant sex (all male; age details referenced in Table 1), cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3-T), and processing software (SPM8). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met, and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity and meets several inclusion criteria (I4: within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral control; I5: reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with correction; I6: whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures; I7: reports participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software). However, it does NOT meet I3: the cue modality used in the fMRI task is personalized audiotaped imagery (audio scripts) rather than visual stimuli. Therefore it fails the required inclusion criterion I3. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I3. Exclusion criteria met: none.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the meta-analysis requires fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, but this study used individualized guided-imagery auditory scripts (audio/imagery) to evoke alcohol cues rather than visual cue presentation. The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I4 (it includes within-participant Alcohol-cue > Neutral contrast), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses with FWE correction), I6 (whole-brain results are clearly described and reported), and I7 (reports participant demographics, cue type [alcohol], scanner field strength [3T], and processing software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based solely on failure to satisfy I3 (visual-stimulus requirement).

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual/audio-visual stimuli. The manuscript reports within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > nonsmoking control stimuli, and a group-level whole-brain analysis was conducted (followed by small-volume correction within a priori ROIs) with peak coordinates and figures reported. Relevant study details are provided: participant sex and age comparisons, cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (SPM8 and ASL toolbox). Thus it meets all listed inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-subject task activation maps. The supplied full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (smoking vs neutral images and smoking vs baseline) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (statistical parametric maps with voxelwise thresholds, cluster sizes, coordinate tables and figures). Relevant methodological details are provided (participant age/sex matching reported in tables, cue type = smoking/nicotine, scanner field strength = 3T, processing software = BrainVoyager QX). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual photographic cues and within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > control cues). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with tables/figures of coordinates and reports scanner field strength (4.0 T) and participant age/sex information. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical human task fMRI). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses visual cues paired with a natural reward (juice) to probe reward-related cue processing (temporal-difference/cue events). The authors report within-subject contrasts for event types (CS, UCS, PTDE, NTDE) and group-level voxelwise analyses including whole-brain (WB) results (and SVC), with WB statistical maps and reported clusters. Methods report participant age range, cue type (juice), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Allegra), and processing software (AFNI). Therefore it meets criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity with visual stimuli, within-participant contrasts, whole-brain task-evoked analyses, and required reporting details.

This study is an fMRI investigation of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs neutral images). It reports a within-participant contrast (smoke > neutral) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME 1; threshold Z>2.3, cluster p=0.05) with regions reported in tables/figures. Methods include participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Although the paper includes seed-based PPI connectivity analyses, it also provides unmasked whole-brain task activation results, so it does not meet exclusion criteria for connectivity-only or ROI-only studies. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (meets I3). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > nonalcohol beverage cues (I4) and presents group-level voxelwise statistical mapping using SPM on spatially normalized data with cluster thresholds (group-level task-evoked maps reported in figures and tables), satisfying I5 and I6. The manuscript reports participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (MEDx and SPM99), satisfying I7. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Note: imaging was restricted to anterior brain regions (anterior third), which limits coverage but does not negate that a group-level voxelwise task map was performed and reported. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion under the meta-analysis criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue modality is gustatory (alcohol taste delivered via tubing) rather than visual stimuli required by the meta-analysis objective. The manuscript does satisfy I4 (within-participant alcohol>water contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation with cluster correction), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/tabled/figured), and I7 (reported participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [FSL]). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the cue modality is gustatory (alcohol taste delivery), not visual stimuli, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). The study does meet I4 (within-participant Alcohol>Water contrast), I5 (reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise task maps), I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Overall confidence is high that the study should be excluded on the basis of failing I3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrast (cocaine cues > neutral cues), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME mixed-effects, thresholding reported) with coordinates/cluster results and figures, and reports participant sex counts, matching/age information, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-evoked, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in smokers using visual stimuli (cigarette-related and emotional pictures). The paper reports a within-subject cigarette>neutral contrast using a random-effects, group-level whole-brain analysis (t-maps, cluster results reported in Table 2 and figures). Methods include participant age range and sex breakdown, cue type (nicotine/cigarette pictures), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). All required inclusion criteria (I3–I7) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts (cocaine vs neutral), reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (unbiased second-level t tests with cluster correction), and provides whole-brain results in figures/tables/text. Participant demographics (male, 18–55), cue types (cocaine, sexual, aversive), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only without unmasked task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given these points, the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes visual smoking cue reactivity (videos) and within-subject contrasts (smoking cue vs baseline) as well as alcohol cue contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (voxel-wise one-sample t tests, cluster-wise inference reported). The paper reports participant age/sex summary, cue types (alcohol taste and visual smoking), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (FSL). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core article content is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-subject task activations). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual-stimulus cue-reactivity (it contains qualifying visual cue contrasts for smoking).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) visual cue reactivity using validated cigarette-related videos. It reports within-participant contrasts (crave-allow vs neutral; crave-resist vs neutral) and longitudinal before-to-after treatment contrasts, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using FSL/FLAME and cluster correction; results are presented as figures and tables of coordinates. Scanner field strength (1.5 T), cue type (nicotine), and processing software (FSL) are reported; demographic/treatment variables (including sex and other baseline demographics) are described and tabulated. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and not non-empirical). Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual stimulus cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This study does not assess visual drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity (I3 not met). It uses a probabilistic delay-discounting task with monetary rewards rather than presentation of alcohol or other drug/food/sexual cues, and thus contains no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4 not met). The manuscript does include group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures (I5 and I6 met). It also reports scanner field strength and processing software but does not present the required cue type (drug/natural reward visual stimuli) as specified (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) and includes within-subject contrasts of craved food > control stimuli (Look Craved > Look Not Craved and Look Craved > Look Neutral). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (AlphaSim-corrected, tables of coordinates provided), and relevant participant and scanner/method details are reported (age/sex, food cue type, 3.0T Siemens Allegra, SPM8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking (nicotine) cues with within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > neutral cues), conducted with voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses and whole-brain reporting (tables/figures and supplementary materials). The paper reports participant age and sex, cue type, scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM5). Methods, results, and discussion are present and complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and appetitive/neutral visual control stimuli, explicitly examining decisions-to-drink. The analyses include within-participant contrasts of alcohol versus control stimuli (alcohol > food/items) and higher-level group comparisons, reported as whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-corrected maps) using FSL. The manuscript reports participant age range and sex (women aged 18–28), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (FSL v4.1.9). Results are described in the text with figures and coordinate-based reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for an fMRI cue-reactivity meta-analysis of drug/natural reward-related visual stimuli.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with visual cues indicating monetary rewards/loss-avoidance (natural rewards). It reports within-subject contrasts of reward-anticipation versus non-incentive (reward>non-reward) and other task contrasts. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps and voxelwise t-tests are reported (familywise-corrected activations, tables/figures described). Participant age/sex, cue type (money), scanner field strength (3 T) and processing software (AFNI) are provided. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task activation maps). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol images (with a sip prime) and reports within-subject contrasts (Alcohol > Beverage; Alcohol > Control). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were generated and thresholded (SPM96/MEDx; Talairach normalization), with results presented in tables/figures (coordinates and cluster-level thresholds). Participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue-reactivity paradigm used gustatory (taste) stimuli delivered via a gustometer (alcohol vs. juice), not visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant Alcohol>Control contrast: Alcohol vs. Juice), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported for correlations with methylation), I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Because the meta-analysis specifically requires visual cue-based paradigms, this gustatory-cue study must be excluded.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study using visual smoking (nicotine) cues (videos) and reports within-participant Cigarette Cues > Neutral Cues contrasts. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (cluster-corrected) and reports results in tables and figures. Relevant methodological details are provided (participant age range and sex collected, cue type, scanner field strength = 3T, and processing software = FSL). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of visual heroin-related cues in methadone-maintained patients and meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it is a functional MRI study using visual drug-related stimuli; (I4) it includes within-participant contrasts (heroin-related > neutral) and reports predose vs postdose comparisons; (I5/I6) group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (one-sample and paired t tests, thresholding and cluster extent reported, activation maps and tables referenced); (I7) participant age/sex, cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (FSL/FMRIB tools) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text contains introduction/background, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Full text is complete. Exclusion reason: The study does not meet I3. Although this is an fMRI within-subject study that tested reward>neutral contrasts (I4 met), reports group-level whole-brain task and PPI results with coordinates (I5 and I6 met), and provides participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength and processing software (I7 met), it does not assess cue-reactivity to the review’s target drug or natural reward cue types. The task used monetary cues (monetary reward/neutral/punishment), not drug-related (e.g., nicotine cues) or the natural reward categories specified in the meta-analysis (e.g., food, sexual). Thus I3 (fMRI assessing drug or natural reward–related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos of cocaine and food). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of cocaine > food cues, provides voxel-wise whole-brain activation results (cluster maps, corrected thresholds, and supplemental tables/figures), and describes participant age/sex, cue types (cocaine, food), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T) and processing software (AFNI). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and should be included.

The study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. The meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity assessed using visual stimuli (I3); this study used personalized guided imagery presented auditorily (script-driven mental imagery), not visual cue presentation, so I3 is not met. The study’s analyses focus on functional connectivity (intrinsic connectivity distribution and seed-to-voxel connectivity) during imagery rather than on task-evoked, within-participant contrasts of cue>control producing whole-brain activation maps (I4 and I5 are not met). The paper does report participant demographics, cue type (food), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (SPM5, BioImage Suite), so I7 is met. Because the report contains only connectivity analyses without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map, it meets exclusion criterion E4 (studies reporting only connectivity/resting-state analyses without whole-brain task activation). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore, the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Full text appears to be only the abstract (fulltext_incomplete=true). Based on the abstract: it is an fMRI study of cannabis visual cue-reactivity with within-subject cannabis>neutral contrasts and reports whole-brain task-evoked results (regions and cluster threshold), so I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. However, key reporting required by I7 (participant age and sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software) is incompletely reported in the provided content (sex reported but no ages, scanner field strength, or processing software). Because I7 is not met and the full text is incomplete, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This is not an fMRI study: it is a TMS/EMG study measuring motor-evoked potentials in response to visual smoking cues. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for fMRI cue-reactivity data. Specifically, inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a functional MRI study), I4 (no within-participant fMRI contrast of drug cues > control), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I6 (no whole-brain fMRI results reported), I7 (MRI scanner field strength and processing software not reported because no MRI was used). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E3–E6) are directly applicable. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (images) and water controls in detoxified alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol versus water stimuli in the PIT task (alcohol>water parametric modulators). The manuscript reports exploratory whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (coordinates, cluster size, and pFWE−SVC values) in addition to ROI analyses. Participant age and sex summaries are provided, cue type is alcohol, scanner field strength (Siemens Trio 3T) and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) are present; fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore all required inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and the study is included.

This task-based fMRI study investigates cocaine and natural reward (erotic) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts (drug-related vs. neutral) and participant details (age/sex), scanner field strength, and processing software. However, the primary neuroimaging results are reported via independent component analysis (ICA) and GLMs on component time courses (network-level effects). The manuscript does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (e.g., voxelwise drug>neutral GLM results); instead, results reflect ICA component maps and component modulation statistics. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ICA/network analyses without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map), and by extension I6 (not applicable because no qualifying whole-brain results are provided). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (participants held and viewed cigarettes vs neutral objects). It includes within-participant contrasts of cigarette>neutral cues (repeated-measures voxel-wise ANOVA with a main effect of cue), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables/coordinates, and provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (NIS, AFNI). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking cues (videos) that performed within-subject contrasts of smoking cues (SC) versus non-smoking control stimuli and reported group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM2 (random-effects second-level analyses). Results are reported with coordinates and figures; participant age, sex breakdown, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM2) are provided. Full manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3–I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues (I3 satisfied). The analysis includes a within-subject contrast CUEalc > IAPSneutral (I4 satisfied). Group-level, voxelwise random-effects second-level analyses (SPM/BPM) were performed and whole-brain corrected results are reported (e.g., whole-brain FWE P values and coordinates), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (I5,I6 satisfied). The paper reports participant age/sex matching, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM8, VBM8, BPM), meeting I7. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state only, and provides whole-brain task activation maps. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual (word) stimuli and reports an individual-level cocaine>neutral contrast and standard preprocessing/analysis with SPM8 (I3, I4 satisfied). Participant/sample, scanner (3T), cue type (cocaine), and software are reported (I7 satisfied). However, the paper reports region-of-interest (ROI) based small-volume-corrected group analyses for the cocaine>neutral contrast and explicitly reports no significant ROI results; there is no reported unmasked, whole-brain group-level cocaine>neutral statistical map available in the main text (results focus on ROI/SVC and supplementary ROI-based figures). Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group map required for inclusion. Exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked map).

This article is a human fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) in alcohol-dependent participants, reporting within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > non-alcohol beverage controls. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM5; uncorrected p<.005 with cluster extent threshold) with results described in text, tables and figures. Relevant methodological details are provided: cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (Philips 3.0T), and processing software (SPM5). Participant demographics (age/sex) are referenced in Table 1 and described in the text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue-reactivity (drug, sexual, aversive, neutral) in patients with opioid use disorder. The methods include within-subject contrasts of drug versus neutral stimuli and group-level analyses. The authors report a whole-brain voxelwise session × stimulus ANOVA with corrected thresholds and provide cluster coordinates for significant effects (ventral striatum/mOFC). Participant age and sex are reported, cue types are specified (opioid/heroin; sexual; aversive), scanner field strength (Siemens Tim Trio 3T) and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject smoking>control contrasts, but the voxelwise analyses were performed within an a priori mask (regions previously associated with cue-reactivity) rather than as an unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise task map. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for a whole-brain group-level statistical map (I5). It does meet I3 (fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity with visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant smoking>control contrast), I6 (results reported in tables/figures described in text), and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength 1.5T, and SPM2 processing reported). Full text appears complete. Exclusion criteria specific to ROI-only or connectivity-only reports (E3/E4/E5/E6) do not apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses visual cue videos (food and cocaine) to probe reward-related cue-reactivity in humans. It reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine>neutral and food>neutral), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with cluster-level FWE correction, and presents coordinates/figures/tables of results. Participant age and sex (20 males, mean age reported), cue types, MRI field strength (4 T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual smoking and food clips and reports within-subject Smoke vs Food contrasts using ICA-derived component betas. However, it does not present a group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain task activation map (or tables of voxelwise coordinates for a smoke>control or food>control GLM contrast). Instead, analyses are based on group ICA components and temporal sorting (network/component-level betas). According to the review exclusion criteria, studies that report only ICA/other connectivity or component-based analyses without a whole-brain task activation map must be excluded (E4). The paper does meet other inclusion points (I3, I4, I7) but fails I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), so it must be excluded.

This study reports fMRI BOLD responses to visual affective stimuli and alcohol/neutral beverage images in alcohol-dependent patients, but the provided full text does not clearly report critical methodological details required by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study with visual drug/natural reward cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain results appear to be reported, as indicated by references to Fig. 4 and table S3), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the provided text does not explicitly present a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli in a clearly described way), and I7 (essential reporting items such as MRI scanner field strength and processing software are not present in the provided full text; sex distribution is not clearly reported either). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I4 and I7 are not clearly met in the available full text, the study must be excluded. If the supplementary materials (table S3, methods) contain the missing scanner/software and explicit alcohol>neutral contrasts, re-screening with the complete materials could change this decision.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual high-calorie food cues (natural reward). It reports within-subject contrasts of high-calorie food images > non-food control images, and performs group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (exploratory whole-brain comparisons and correlations reported with MNI coordinates and Table 1). Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM99) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This empirical fMRI study used visual cannabis cues and included within-subject contrasts of cannabis images > neutral/control images. Group-level, whole-brain task effects are reported (main effects per group whole-brain corrected, and between-group results reported with appropriate ROI and whole-brain corrections), with results presented in tables and figures. Relevant methodological details are provided (participant ages/sex, cue type = cannabis, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software = FSL/FEAT). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol beverage pictures). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > control (alcpic > con) and other cue contrasts. Analyses were whole-brain random-effects group-level voxelwise maps (SPM8) with cluster correction and report coordinates/tables/figures of activations (Tables 2–4, figures). Participant information (n=26 ALC, 26 controls), age-matching, sex matching, scanner field strength (GE 3T), and processing software (SPM8) are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task activation maps, is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol images). It includes within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs. non-alcohol and alcohol vs. degraded images), reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-based multiple comparison correction and tables/figures of significant clusters, and provides participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T Allegra), and processing software (SPM5). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or task-effect absent) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues in a go/no-go task with within-subject contrasts (e.g., Alcohol_nogo > Non-alcohol_go; interaction contrasts) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses reported (cluster-FWE corrected, tables/figures with coordinates). Participant demographics (age, sex proportions), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant alcohol>beverage contrasts (within-group alcohol vs beverage) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted with SPM99. Whole-brain results are reported (figures and Talairach coordinates/t-scores in Table 3) and scanner field strength (3.0 T), processing software (SPM99), cue type (alcohol), and participant sex are described. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effect, empirical human fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues versus neutral cues, reporting within-participant heroin-related > neutral contrasts and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM8; Monte Carlo/AFNI Alphasim correction). Participant demographics (male subjects; age reported), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software are all provided. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes unmasked whole-brain task effects). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (drug-related) with detoxified alcohol-dependent participants and healthy controls. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol-associated > control stimuli, performed at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM99 analyses (thresholds and cluster sizes reported), and presents coordinate tables and figures. Participant age and sex are reported (all male; ages given), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM99). The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine-dependent participants using visual smoking-related cues vs matched neutral images. The authors report within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral) for encoding and retrieval phases, and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed model, cluster-corrected across the entire brain) with coordinates presented in Table 2 and figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are all reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (AFNI), the paper’s group-level analyses were conducted within a priori ROIs (5-mm spheres) rather than reporting any unmasked, whole‑brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking > neutral cues (crave and resist conditions). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FEAT/FLAME in FSL; Z>2.3, cluster p=0.05) and results are reported with cluster tables and MNI coordinates. Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without whole-brain task map, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli with an ALC>BEV within-subject contrast and reports participant age/sex, scanner (3T), and processing software (FSL). However, the imaging analyses reported are ROI-based (ventral striatum percent signal change) and the full text does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinate tables/whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Design: randomized, double-blind, cross-over within-subjects fMRI study where participants viewed highly desirable food, less-desirable food, and non-food images. Analyses: first-level contrasts (highly desirable > less desirable; all food > non-food) were taken to second-level paired t-tests comparing walnut vs placebo, using SPM8 and reporting whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster- and peak-level statistics) with coordinate (32,10,10) and FWE-corrected p-values. Participant details (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion requirements for this meta-analysis: it did not use visual drug or natural reward cues (fails I3) and did not include a within-participant contrast of visual drug-cue > control stimuli (fails I4). Instead, the study used auditory script-based guided imagery to induce stress and stress-induced cocaine craving and contrasted stress vs neutral imagery. The study does meet I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps and coordinate tables), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/tabled), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type [stress-induced cocaine craving], MRI field strength [1.5T], and processing software [MATLAB/Yale fMRI package]). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity investigation using visual alcohol images and includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol cues vs non-alcoholic beverage controls). It reports participant age range, sex demographics, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT). However, the imaging analyses and primary results are based on an a priori right ventral striatum ROI (extraction of percent signal change) rather than presenting any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinate results. Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain task activation evidence and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion ID met: E3. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain maps).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cannabis (marijuana) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, reporting within-subject MJ cue > non-MJ cue contrasts at the group (random-effects) voxelwise level. The paper describes whole-brain preprocessing and GLM analyses in SPM2 and reports voxelwise results as tables of coordinates and statistical maps (including an interactive unmasked display), with cluster-corrected thresholds applied (ROI mask used for correction but voxelwise contrasts were performed and reported). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (cannabis), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual tobacco advertisement stimuli (visual cues) and reports within-subject contrasts (tobacco > control advertisements). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM5; cluster-level FDR-corrected maps and supporting tables/ROIs are described). Key participant details (male sex, ages), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: the study includes whole-brain task activation maps (not ROI-only), is not a connectivity- or resting-state-only study, and provides task-evoked within-participant contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues with a within-subject contrast (heroin-related > neutral), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects FLAME, cluster correction). Demographics (age, sex), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines cannabis cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (cannabis word Stroop) and reports within-subject contrasts (cannabis > neutral) with detailed participant, scanner (3T) and SPM8 processing information. However, all fMRI analyses were restricted to a priori ROIs with small-volume corrections and peak coordinates; no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps or whole-brain results are reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI drug cue-reactivity with visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant drug cues > control contrast), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, processing software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked map). Full text appears complete.

This study used resting-state fMRI (rsFC) to compare smokers and non-smokers and to examine dependence-related differences; it did not present any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual stimuli nor any within-participant contrasts of drug-cues > control stimuli. No group-level whole-brain, task-evoked statistical maps (voxelwise task activation) are reported. Therefore it does not meet the core inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity. Exclusion ID met: E4 (study reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without task activation). Inclusion ID met: I7 (the paper reports participant age and sex, cue type = nicotine, scanner field strength = 3.0 T, and processing software DPARSF). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrast), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I6 (not applicable because no task whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (food > control) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper reports SPM5-based second-level whole-brain results (FDR-corrected and uncorrected thresholds), tables/figures of activated clusters, and extracted region-level data. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue modality is tactile (tactile presentations of a marijuana pipe and a pencil), not visual stimuli required by the review. The paper does meet several other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrast: marijuana cues > control cues), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses using FLAME/FSL with cluster-corrected maps), I6 (whole-brain results are described and reported as clusters/tables/figures), and I7 (reports participant age/sex information, cue type=cannabis, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software FSL). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is an empirical fMRI paper using visual alcohol cues and neutral control images, reporting within-participant contrasts ('favourite drinks > neutral') and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with coordinate tables. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3 T) and processing software (SPM5) are reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity visual studies and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study in smokers using visual smoking-related and matched neutral images (nicotine cue type). The paper reports within-subject event types and t-contrasts (smoking vs neutral), and a group-level random-effects (second-level) whole-brain voxelwise analysis (SPM2) with reported activation clusters (tables/figures). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software are reported. Although the smoking>neutral contrast did not yield significant activations, the required within-participant contrast and whole-brain group analysis were performed and reported. Full text is complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is a whole-brain fMRI investigation of alcohol cue reactivity but uses gustatory (taste) cues (alcohol taste vs. litchi juice) rather than visual stimuli, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I3 (visual stimuli). Additionally, the full text does not report the MRI scanner field strength (e.g., 1.5T or 3T), so it fails inclusion criterion I7, which requires reporting of scanner field strength along with other methodological details. The study does satisfy other inclusions: it reports a within-participant alcohol>control contrast (I4), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and cluster-corrected maps with coordinate tables (I5, I6), and reports participant age/sex, cue type, and processing software. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded because it does not use visual cue stimuli (I3) and does not report scanner field strength (I7).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures and a taste) in humans. It reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs beverage) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 (thresholded maps, reported in tables and figures). Relevant methodological details are provided (scanner field strength 1.5T, processing software SPM2), and participant demographics are reported (Table 1). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is an fMRI investigation of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual smoking cues in smokers. It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking vs neutral cues (pre- vs post-rTMS) and group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses with coordinates and cluster statistics (e.g., mOFC, NAc, ACC). Methods include participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (SPM8). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-subject whole-brain activation maps). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using smoking-related visual stimuli (nicotine cues). The methods report within-participant contrasts of smoking vs. neutral cues, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with reported statistical maps and peak coordinates, and relevant participant details (male adults), cue type (smoking/nicotine), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM5). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing complete assessment. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, contains within-subject whole-brain task contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual drug cues (smoking) that satisfies all inclusion criteria. I3: The study uses fMRI to assess smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity with visual stimuli. I4: It includes a within-participant contrast (smoking cues > neutral stimuli) at the individual level, carried forward to group analysis. I5/I6: Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM99 and results are reported as statistical parametric maps and tables/figures (voxelwise regression, conjunction). I7: Participant age and sex (ten male smokers, mean age 32), cue type (nicotine/smoking), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM99) are reported. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports only region-of-interest analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (event-related fMRI of drug-related cue-reactivity using visual smoking images), I4 (within-participant contrast of smoking cues > neutral control images reported), I7 (reported participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software details). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported; analyses were ROI-based), I6 (not applicable because whole-brain results were not provided in tables/figures/text). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because the study only reports ROI analyses without accompanying unmasked, whole-brain task activation maps, it fails the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain results and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcohol-related pictures) and includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol vs neutral). A group-level, whole-brain second-level ANOVA was performed and voxelwise results (significant posterior cingulate cluster) are reported and thresholded, with results described in text and figures. Scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (AFNI) are reported; participant demographics are referenced in Table 1 (demographic characteristics presented). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This fMRI study used oral alcohol tastes with preceding visual word cues, but the reported within-participant contrasts focus on taste outcomes and prediction error (e.g., alcohol taste vs. water taste; positive PE) rather than a cue-phase visual drug-cue > control-cue contrast. The paper does not present a whole-brain, within-subject contrast of alcohol visual cue > water visual cue that would index visual cue-reactivity. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control stimuli contrast) and does not clearly satisfy I3 for cue-reactivity using visual stimuli as the primary assessed effect. The study does provide whole-brain voxelwise results (I5), reports coordinates/figures (I6), and includes participant, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software details (I7). Full text appears complete.

Only the article abstract is provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). The abstract describes an fMRI study of nicotine cue exposure in virtual environments, so I3 (fMRI study using visual cue-like virtual environments) appears satisfied. However, the manuscript as provided lacks critical methodological/results details needed to confirm inclusion: no clear within-participant contrast of drug cues>control stimuli (I4 not confirmed), no explicit report of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or coordinate tables/figures (I5/I6 not confirmed), and key reporting items (participant sex, MRI field strength, processing software) are missing (I7 not met). Because required inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7 cannot be verified from the incomplete text, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis at this stage. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on the abstract alone.

The available record appears to be only an abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract the study is an fMRI task using visual heroin cues and reports activated brain areas, so it meets I3 (fMRI visual cue-reactivity) and I6 (results described in text). However, key details required by the inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the abstract: I4 (explicit within-participant drug cues>control contrast) is not clearly reported; I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map) is not explicitly confirmed despite reporting regions; and I7 (reporting participant age plus sex, cue type, scanner strength, and processing software) is partially reported—sex, cue type, scanner field strength and software are present but participant ages are not. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because the core full text (methods, full results, and maps/coordinates) is not available, I cannot verify all inclusion criteria; per instructions fulltext_incomplete takes precedence and I therefore exclude. Recommend retrieving the complete article to reassess inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images signalling impending chocolate milk vs tasteless solution). The study reports within-subject contrasts (anticipation: chocolate milk cue vs tasteless cue; receipt: chocolate milk vs tasteless solution) and group-level, random-effects voxelwise analyses (including whole-brain regression and reporting of T-maps). Relevant metadata are provided (participant ages/sex matching, cue type = food, scanner field strength = 3.0 T, processing software = SPM8). Whole-brain results and ROI-corrected results are described and thresholding/statistical procedures are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core article content is present.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage images). It reports within-participant contrasts (alcoholic > non-alcoholic beverages) and performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI; 3T scanner) with family-wise error correction. Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength, and processing software are described. Although the alcohol-cue contrast yielded no significant clusters (null result), the whole-brain analyses for the cue conditions were conducted and described in the text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Note: coordinates for alcohol cue activations are not reported because results were null, but this does not preclude inclusion per the stated criteria.

Full text is unavailable (website returns an error page). Cannot verify whether the study meets inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI with visual drug/natural reward cues) not confirmed; I4 (within-participant contrast of drug-cues>control) not confirmed; I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) not confirmed; I6 (whole-brain results clearly described) not confirmed; I7 (reporting participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software) not confirmed. Therefore no inclusion criteria can be confirmed as met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confirmed as met either. Because the full text is incomplete/unavailable, exclude per protocol (fulltext_incomplete).

The full text is a task-based fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts (smoke vs neutral/rest). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise maps; figures and supplementary results/tables referenced), and provides participant age/sex information, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8/TBV). The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is a resting-state functional connectivity study of alexithymia and tobacco craving, not a task-based cue-reactivity fMRI study using visual drug/natural reward cues. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state / seed-based connectivity analyses without any task-evoked whole-brain activation map). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI cue-reactivity paradigm with visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I6 (no task whole-brain results reported in any form), I7 (while participant age/sex and scanner field strength are reported, there is no reporting of a cue-type task or processing software in the context of a cue-reactivity task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Only the abstract is provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). The abstract indicates an fMRI study with a visual 'heroin puffing' movie cue, so I3 (fMRI study assessing drug-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) appears satisfied. However, the abstract does not report whether a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli was performed (I4), nor does it confirm the presence of group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate/figure reporting (I5/I6). Participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software are not reported in the abstract (I7). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify the remaining required inclusion criteria; therefore the study is excluded pending retrieval of the full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (vs soft-drink control) in alcohol-dependent patients and controls. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol vs neutral (via the interaction (approach alcohol>avoid alcohol)>(approach soft drink>avoid soft drink) and separate approach contrasts), includes group-level second-level (two-sample t-test) voxelwise analyses, and refers to whole-brain results (Supplementary Table S1). Key participant details (age, sex), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for an fMRI cue-reactivity meta-analysis and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and within-subject contrasts of food > control pictures. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM5 (whole-brain thresholds and small-volume corrections are reported) and results are presented in text, figures, and tables. Participant characteristics (age, sex, BMI), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to natural rewards using visual stimuli.

Full text is incomplete: provided content contains only acknowledgments and references, with no Introduction, Methods, Results, or Discussion. Therefore I cannot verify inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none verifiable. Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I3 (unclear from available text whether full fMRI methods and visual food-cue paradigm details are reported), I4 (no accessible information about within-participant contrasts of food cues > control), I5/I6 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables are available in the provided content), I7 (participant demographics, cue type details, scanner field strength, and processing software are not reported in the provided text). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 can be confidently applied from the available excerpt. Action: EXCLUDE due to incomplete/full-text not provided; request full article to reassess.

This is an fMRI task-based study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (drug-related words). It reports within-subject contrasts (drug vs. neutral words) and group analyses, and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds, coordinates, and tables) analyzed with SPM2 on a 4T scanner. Participant demographics and cue type are reported (see Table S1), scanner field strength and processing software are specified. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity (food) that uses visual stimuli (also auditory) and reports within-participant contrasts (food>nonfood and high-ED>low-ED). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps carried out with SPM5 and reported via tables/figures (cluster thresholds and coordinates provided). Participant age, sex (female), cue type (food high-/low-energy density), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM5) are clearly reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria: it is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue (a drug-related, natural reward-related cue category: alcohol) reactivity using visual stimuli (video of alcohol drinking). The analysis includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol video vs mosaic control) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM/RFX results (FDR-corrected clusters reported and a Table of brain areas). Relevant methodological details are provided: participant demographics (age and sex reported in demographics), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant task activation maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I include the study.

This study examines fMRI responses to smoking video cues (visual drug-related stimuli) and includes within-participant comparisons (smoking vs. nonsmoking blocks) and reports participant demographics, scanner (3T) and processing software (SPM8). However, the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map for drug cues > control stimuli; results focus on ROI-based activity measures and seed-based functional connectivity maps. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only seed-based connectivity/ROI-focused analyses without an unmasked whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete.

This study includes an fMRI task using visual drug cues (drug words) and reports within-participant contrasts (drug > neutral; drug > fixation). It reports scanner field strength (4T), processing software (SPM8), participant sex counts, and cue type (cocaine). However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the drug>control contrast; fMRI results are presented via ROI extractions (OFC, ventral striatum) and the text does not provide whole-brain task activation coordinates or maps. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results).

This article reports an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual alcohol stimuli and reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral/control cues. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps and coordinate tables/figures are reported (e.g., contrasts “alcohol–neutral stimuli”, tables and images described). Participant/sample information (recruited 76 abstinent alcohol-dependent patients; demographic/clinical characteristics referenced in Table 1), cue type (alcohol), and fMRI acquisition/analysis are described (with details in supplementary material), satisfying reporting requirements.
