The study is empirical, task-based fMRI (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), and presents task-evoked whole-brain results appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of visual reward-related cue reactivity. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of visual nicotine (smoking) cues with within-subject SCs vs NCs contrasts and reports coordinates and figures; participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner (1.5T) and software (SPM2) are reported. However, group-level results are reported within an a priori fronto-limbic mask rather than as an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. Therefore it constitutes a region-restricted/ROI-style analysis and does not provide whole-brain group-level maps required by the meta-analysis. Exclusion ID E3 applies. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I6, I7. Inclusion ID not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (movie scenes). It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking > control scenes, reports a group-level, whole-brain random-effects (voxelwise) analysis (smoking vs control) and presents results in figures/tables. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are documented. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effect, and is empirical). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based analyses and does not provide group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports only region-of-interest analyses with no whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrast ALC>BEV [ALC–BEV] reported), I7 (participant age/sex info, cue type [alcohol], MRI scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [FSL] are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of reward-related cues (monetary and cigarette) using visual task cues and within-subject contrasts (money > neutral; puff > neutral), and reports sufficient participant and scanner details. However, all reported neuroimaging results focus on a priori ROI analyses (ventral/dorsal striatum) and extracted eigenvariates from these ROI clusters; the manuscript does not present unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of drug/natural reward-related cues using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrasts of cue>control), I6 (whole-brain results acceptable in tables/figures — N/A but satisfied formatting allowance), and I7 (reported age/sex, cue type, field strength, processing software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain, unmasked task activation map reported). Conclusion: EXCLUDE (E3).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual photographic stimuli. It includes within-participant smoking cue > control cue contrasts, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects multiple regression) with tables/figures of significant clusters. Relevant participant information (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual smoking-related cues (nicotine) that: (1) used within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > neutral control stimuli; (2) conducted group-level, whole-brain (random-effects GLM) voxelwise analyses for the cue task; (3) reported whole-brain results in the text and figures (even if cue effects did not survive correction); and (4) reported relevant methodological/participant details including participant sex (all male), cue type (smoking/nicotine), MRI field strength (3T) and processing software (BrainVoyager). Participant demographics are referenced in Table 1 (age/other details). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task contrasts, and is original human fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue modality is olfactory (ethanol odor), not visual. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (within-participant contrast: ethanol odor > neutral air), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported using SPM), I6 (whole-brain results described in text/figures/tables), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type=alcohol, MRI field strength=1.5T, and processing software=SPM are reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E6 violations). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded solely because I3 (visual stimuli) is not met.

This study is a resting-state seed-based functional connectivity (habenula–striatum) imaging study in psychiatric inpatients and does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, nor does it include any within-participant task contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli or a whole-brain task-evoked statistical map. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrast), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain task results reported), I7 (does not report cue type or task-related cue details required for the review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This empirical fMRI study used visual heroin-related and neutral pictures (event-related cue-reactivity task), modeled a within-subject contrast (heroin>neutral) at first level and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses reporting task-evoked activations (clusters/coordinates reported, P<0.001 uncorrected). Methods report participant age/sex (all male, ages reported), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). Although the paper also includes resting-state seed-based connectivity, it clearly reports whole-brain task activation maps; no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food: chocolate) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of chocolate) and oral delivery. It includes within-participant contrasts of reward cues versus control (e.g., chocpic vs. grey visual control) and other relevant contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM2), with coordinates and cluster-wise/voxel-wise corrections described and figures/tables referenced. Key participant details (age range 20–30, all female), cue type (food/chocolate), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM2) are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes whole-brain task activation maps, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study used olfactory (smell) cues as the primary stimuli during fMRI (alcohol odors vs control odors). Although pictures were shown during a pre-scan familiarization, no visual stimuli were presented during the actual imaging runs (subjects had eyes closed), so the fMRI cue-reactivity data are not based on visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant AO>ApCO contrasts), I5 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses reported), I6 (whole-brain results described/figured), I7 (participant info, cue type, 3T scanner, SPM5 processing reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion relevant to assessment.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs non-alcohol beverage images) with a within-subject ALC>BEV contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level GLM) are reported (cluster-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures) using SPM8 on a 3T scanner. Participant age range and sex distributions, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues and reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) with group-level voxelwise whole-brain results; however, the provided full text does not report participant sex information. Inclusion criterion I7 requires relevant information for age AND sex (plus cue type, scanner strength, and processing software). Age, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM5) are reported, but sex is not described in the provided text; therefore not all inclusion criteria are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual alcohol (drug) and natural reward stimuli (I3) and it reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps (e.g., win>lose) with results presented in figures/tables (I5, I6) and provides participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (I7), the paper does not present a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward cues > control stimuli (I4). The analyses focus on reward (win>lose) and high vs low personal reference, and stimulus-category effects are reported via ANOVAs, but no unmasked alcohol>neutral (or food>neutral) cue-reactivity whole-brain contrast is provided. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 required for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The full text is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual smoking videos. It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking>control videos and reports group-level, voxelwise t-maps (mixed-effects) thresholded for whole-brain inference and lists peak coordinates in tables/figures. Participant age and sex are reported (mean age, sexes), cue type (smoking/nicotine), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software (fmristat). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli experimentally conditioned to alcohol (novel geometric CS). The study performed within-subject contrasts between CS+ and CS− (CS+ > CS− and CS− > CS+), conducted group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM5 analyses with FWE cluster correction and reported peak coordinates/tables and figures. Participant age and sex (heavy-drinking males, mean age reported), cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7 and should be included.

This study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps processed with SPM8 on a 3T scanner, and provides participant age/sex and cue type (alcohol). However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control (neutral) stimuli: all stimuli were alcohol-related and the primary analyses compare instruction conditions (prayer vs passive/news) rather than alcohol images versus neutral or control images. Although condition>baseline contrasts are reported, no alcohol>neutral cue contrast is present, so inclusion criterion I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I4. Exclusion criteria applied: none.

Full text is complete. Excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the alcohol cue was delivered as a gustatory (taste) stimulus (liquid alcohol vs isocaloric control) rather than a visual alcohol cue. Although the study includes visual presentation of participant statements, the cue-reactivity contrast of interest (alcohol vs control) used taste stimuli. The study does meet I4 (within-participant alcohol>control cue contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and visualized), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type = alcohol, 3T scanner field strength, processing software FSL reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded due to failure to satisfy I3 (visual-stimulus cue requirement).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues. It reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol > non-alcoholic beverage) and other stimulus contrasts, and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests and 2×3 ANOVA, voxel-wise thresholds and family-wise error correction reported). Results are reported with coordinate tables and figures. Relevant methodological details are provided: participant groups (age- and gender-matched; see Table 1), cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (AFNI). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This empirical fMRI study used visual drug-related (alcohol, marijuana, polydrug) picture cues in college students and reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral, polydrug>neutral, marijuana>neutral). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (FEAT/FSL) with reported tables and figures of activations. The paper reports participant age and sex, cue types, scanner field strength (Siemens Allegra 3T), and processing software (FSL). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes methods, results and discussion; thus fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The GLM included within-subject regressors for high-calorie, low-calorie, and non-food images and task contrasts (condition × task) were tested using group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (LME, FWE whole-brain correction) reported in figures and text. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3 T), and processing software (BioImageSuite/AFNI). Whole-brain statistical maps (FWE-corrected) are presented, satisfying voxelwise group-level reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are violated. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related cues and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses of responses to alcohol, polydrug, and marijuana picture cues. However, the primary reported contrasts assess repetition priming (non-studied > studied cues) rather than cue-reactivity contrasts of drug cues > control/neutral stimuli. The paper does not present a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast (I4 not met). Also, relevant reporting is incomplete for inclusion criterion I7: participant age and MRI field strength are not provided in this full text (they are deferred to an accompanying main study), so the required methodological details are not clearly reported here. Whole-brain results and coordinates are reported (satisfying I5 and I6), and it is an fMRI study with visual drug cues (I3). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore exclude.

This is a pharmacological resting-state fMRI pilot in abstinent heroin users comparing KB220Z™ vs placebo; it does not involve a visual cue-reactivity task or cue presentation. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (reports only resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control or natural-reward-cue>control contrast), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I6 (no task-based whole-brain results of cue reactivity reported), I7 (does report age/sex, scanner field strength, and software but does not report a cue/stimulus type or cue-related task). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded for not meeting required task-based cue-reactivity inclusion criteria.

Exclusion met: E3 — the study reports only ROI-based analyses (percent signal change extracted from ACC ROIs) and does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual smoking images), I4 (within-participant contrasts reported: smoke>rest and comparisons with neutral blocks), I7 (participant age/sex reported, cue type = nicotine, 3T scanner field strength, processing software SPM8 reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported), I6 (no whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/supplementary material). Full text appears complete and supplementary material is optional.

E3 applies: the study reports only ROI-based analyses with no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, thus failing the required whole-brain analysis criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > control stimuli reported), I7 (reported participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). I6 is not applicable because no whole-brain results were provided. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (it used aversive fear conditioning with electrical shocks). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses present) and I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (fMRI study of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward cues > control stimuli). I7 is also not met with respect to cue type (the cues are aversive shock-related, not reward/drug cues). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study that used visual alcohol cues (90 pictures of alcoholic and neutral beverages) and emotional visual stimuli, satisfying I3. The authors computed within-participant contrasts (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages) and generated individual and group-level statistical maps, satisfying I4 and I5. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (voxel-wise t-tests) and results are described in the text (I6). Relevant methodological and sample details are reported (age range, sex composition in Table 1; cue type: alcohol; scanner field strength: 3T; processing software: AFNI), satisfying I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This fMRI study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise maps are reported for PE-related activity) and I6 (whole-brain results are clearly described and reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a cue-reactivity study using visual drug/natural reward cues), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli), I7 (does not report a cue type used in the task — task used abstract stimuli with probabilistic reward feedback rather than drug/food/sexual cues). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it does not address the review objective of visual cue-reactivity contrasts.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual stimuli with within-participant food>nonfood contrasts. The paper reports voxel-wise/whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise subtraction, figures, and Table 2 stereotactic coordinates for local maxima), provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (AFNI). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with detoxified alcoholic patients and controls. It includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral, positive>neutral, negative>neutral) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM5 with significance thresholds and reported activations (tables/figures). Participant age, sex, cue types (alcohol, affective/pleasant/negative), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task activation maps). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli that implements within-subject contrasts (alcohol>neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected results, tables/figures and coordinates described). Relevant participant demographics (n, age range, sex), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5/SPM8) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting) are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a behavioral cue-reactivity study using personalized videotaped cues and self-reported urge ratings; it does not include any functional MRI data or analyses. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI whole-brain task activation contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a functional MRI study assessing cue-reactivity with visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant fMRI contrast of drug cues>control), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps), I6 (no whole-brain results reported in any form), I7 (MRI-specific details such as scanner field strength and processing software are not reported). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are specifically triggered (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting), but failure to meet the required inclusion criteria mandates exclusion. Full text appears complete (behavioral methods, results, and discussion present).

Full text is incomplete (only summary/abstract provided). The summary confirms an fMRI study presenting alcohol-associated visual stimuli (meets I3). However, core methodological details are missing: it is not possible to verify a within-participant drug-cue > control contrast (I4 not verifiable), whether group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps were reported (I5 not verifiable), acceptance of coordinate tables/figures (I6 not verifiable), or whether participant demographics, cue type details, scanner field strength, and processing software were reported (I7 not verifiable). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on the summary. Because required inclusion criteria beyond I3 cannot be confirmed from the provided text, I exclude the study pending access to the complete full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (cluster-corrected whole-brain maps with tables/figures) and provides participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Resting-state/ICA analyses are present but the study also includes qualifying task activation maps. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical, within-subject cue-reactivity experiment that reports whole-brain, voxelwise PET activation maps contrasting drug-salient video > neutral video and includes psychophysiological interaction analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast drug cues > control), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). However it fails the critical modality requirement: I3 (requires functional MRI) is not met — this is a PET H2(15)O study, not fMRI. Additionally I7 (requires MRI-specific details such as MRI scanner field strength) is not satisfied as MRI field strength is not applicable/reported for the functional imaging modality used. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore exclude because it does not satisfy I3 (fMRI requirement) and partly fails I7.

Although this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking cues with within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts and reports participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and AFNI processing (meeting I3, I4, I7), the analyses are ROI-based (a priori 4 mm spheres) with outcome prediction using extracted ROI betas and Cox/logistic regressions. The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or coordinate table from a whole-brain analysis. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only analyses without whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using audiovisual visual stimuli (10-min videos). It includes a within-participant contrast of smoking cues > non-smoking control cues, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with cluster-correction and peak coordinates (satisfying whole-brain reporting). Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), MRI scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study (Bjork et al., 2012) investigates neural responses to visual monetary (natural) reward cues using an adapted MID task. It includes within-subject contrasts of reward-predictive cues ($1, $10) versus non-incentive ($0) cues, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (3dMEMA, FDR-corrected) with tables/figures of activation coordinates, and provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study investigates smoking cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and within-subject smoking>control contrasts, and reports participant demographics and scanner/processing details. However, analyses are ROI-based (region-of-interest) and the paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps or whole-brain coordinates/figures of voxelwise results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Exclusion ID E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI of drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrast of smoking cues>control), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (group-level whole-brain statistical map) and I6 (no whole-brain results reported in coordinates/figures). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverage images paired with IAPS images). The paper includes within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol vs. non-alcohol cues (e.g., alcoholic versus non-alcoholic beverage cues paired with positive and negative images). Analyses are voxelwise, group-level whole-brain maps (voxel-wise t-tests with cluster correction) reported in tables/figures. Relevant methodological details are provided (male participants, age-matched groups referenced in Table 1, cue type = alcohol, 3-T scanner, AFNI processing). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core content appears complete.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcohol vs soft drink images) in male alcohol-dependent patients. It reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol>control (e.g., alcohol pull>soft drink pull) at the group level, provides whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with coordinates and whole-brain results reported and discussed), and reports key methodological details (male participants, cue type: alcohol, scanner field strength 3T, processing with SPM8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli that reports within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts and group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with coordinates/tables and details on scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (SPM5). However, the article does not report relevant participant sex information (and does not report mean/actual participant ages—only eligibility age range), so it fails inclusion criterion I7 requiring participant age and sex reporting. Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I7) is not met, the study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: cues were individualized script-driven guided-imagery (auditory/internal imagery), not visual stimuli. Met inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrasts: alcohol cue > neutral), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported with familywise correction), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/figures/tables), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type=alcohol, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is behavioral/psychopharmacological and reports self-report craving and mood in alcoholics using a cue-availability paradigm; it does not involve functional MRI data or report any whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an fMRI study using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant fMRI contrast drug cues > control), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise map), I6 (not applicable — no whole-brain results to report), I7 (no MRI scanner/processing details). Exclusion criteria met: none of the fMRI-specific exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (behavioral methods, results, and conclusions are present). Therefore excluded.

This fMRI study uses visual cigarette and food cues (meets I3), reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (meets I5), and describes whole-brain results in text/figures/tables (meets I6). However, it does not present a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward cues > control stimuli (no neutral/control stimulus contrast reported; I4 not met). Also, the report does not specify MRI scanner field strength in the provided full text (scanner model given but field strength not stated), so required methodological details are incomplete (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cues (images) with a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The manuscript reports whole-brain activation results (smoking vs neutral) and PPI results, provides participant age and sex (young males), cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8, FSL). It is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only analyses, and includes a clear group-level task-evoked whole-brain map (reported with FDR correction and figures/tables). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected activations and coordinate tables/figures). However, the provided full text does not explicitly report MRI scanner field strength or the fMRI processing software used (these details are not present in the Methods as given and appear to be in supporting information if at all). Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criterion I7 (reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, MRI scanner field strength, and processing software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered based on the available content.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cue videos (visual stimuli) and control videos. It computed within-participant contrasts ('smoking videos versus control videos') at first level and carried these to group-level mixed-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with appropriate multiple-comparison correction (TFCE), reporting whole-brain results in text/figures/tables. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is nicotine, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL) are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and includes whole-brain task activation maps). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This article is a narrative review summarizing fMRI and MRS findings rather than reporting original human fMRI data. Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper/review without original human fMRI data) applies. Inclusion criteria are not met: I3 (not an original fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual stimuli) is not met; I4 (no within-participant drug cues>control contrast reported as an original analysis) is not met; I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported from an original dataset) is not met; I6 (not applicable because no original whole-brain results are presented) is not met; I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software are not reported for an original dataset) is not met. The provided full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts of food>neutral. The paper reports group-level whole-brain (exploratory 1-sample t test) task-evoked maps and also ROI analyses; whole-brain results are described in text, tables, and figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a within-subject fMRI study using visual natural-reward stimuli (images of a $100 bill vs a blurry rectangle) and reports a within-participant contrast of reward > nonreward. The analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (thresholded and cluster-corrected) with coordinates and figures reported. Participant age/sex, cue type (money), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are all described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This study is an fMRI investigation that includes visual alcohol cues (90 pictures of alcoholic and neutral beverages) and reports individual-level contrasts (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages) used to generate second-level, group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (AFNI 3dMVM). Whole-brain correction (3dClustSim) was applied and results for alcohol-related stimuli are described (clusters reported; Supplementary Table T1 referenced). Participant age and sex are provided (female, 21–65 years), cue type is alcohol, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (AFNI) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not report only ROI analyses (E3), connectivity-only or resting-state analyses (E4), nor only between-group contrasts without a task effect (E5), and it is an empirical human fMRI study (not excluded by E6). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary materials are referenced. Hence INCLUDED.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward). It reports within-subject contrasts (all food > non-food; high-calorie > low-calorie), conducts whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses with results surviving FWE cluster-corrected thresholds, and provides coordinates and figures. Participant characteristics (age, sex), cue type (food high/low calorie), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli and includes within-subject smoking-cue > control-cue contrasts and appropriate participant and scanner details. However, all reported voxel-wise neuroimaging analyses were conducted within an a priori ROI mask (i.e., restricted to selected anatomical regions) rather than reporting an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Thus it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I7 (reported participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, processing software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain/unmasked voxelwise task map reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual/held cues, includes within-participant contrasts comparing cigarette vs control cues, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation results with stereotaxic coordinates and cluster thresholds. Participant age range and sex (male-only), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI, FSL, etc.) are reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual Pavlovian cues. The study includes within-subject contrasts of food-outcome cues > no-outcome cue and other cue-related contrasts, reports group-level voxelwise analyses (with coordinates and supplementary whole-brain exploratory results noted), and provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting) apply. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This study is a behavioral/clinical pilot study assessing heroin craving using a visual analogue scale in methadone-maintained patients; it does not report any functional MRI acquisition, task-based fMRI analyses, visual cue-reactivity paradigms, within-participant contrasts (e.g., drug-cues > control), or group-level whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore it does not meet the critical neuroimaging inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI study), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrast), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I6 (no whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/supplement), I7 (no MRI scanner field strength or processing software reported). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) specifically apply beyond the failure to meet inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) in adolescents. Inclusion criteria met: (I3) fMRI food cue-reactivity using visual stimuli; (I4) within-participant contrasts are reported (go vs no-go trials comparing unhealthy vs healthy food images, and analyses collapsing across food cues to compare conditions); (I5) whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported with cluster coordinates from 3dMVM; (I6) whole-brain results are clearly described in text and tables/figures; (I7) relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI, ANTs, AFNI 3dMVM) are reported. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Note: control stimuli are healthy food images rather than non-food neutral images, but within-subject cue contrasts are present. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (food images) and reports within-subject contrasts of food>nonfood. The paper describes whole-brain GLM analyses and reports group-level voxelwise results (activation maps and whole-brain regression), with peak coordinates provided. Methods report participant age and sex (male, mean age ~23), cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (SPM8). Results include whole-brain and ROI-corrected findings and coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This fMRI study investigates smoking-related cue pleasantness using visual tobacco images (SP task) within an fMRI protocol and reports whole-brain task maps (for the interoceptive attention task) and resting-state connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study assessing drug cue-related pleasantness using visual stimuli), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the IA task), I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), and I7 (reports age/sex, cue type: nicotine, scanner field strength: 3T, and processing software: AFNI). However, the study does not report any within-participant whole-brain task contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (no task-evoked cue-reactivity contrast map is provided), so I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I4 is absent, the study is excluded.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of methamphetamine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It reports a within-participant Methamphetamine Cue > Control Cue contrast and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<.05). Results are reported with figures and a table of coordinates. The manuscript provides participant age and sex, cue type (methamphetamine), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (FSL). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion: E3 applies — the study reports only ROI-focused and region-restricted voxel-wise analyses (PCC ROI and a voxel-wise analysis restricted to the PCC) and does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the smoking>neutral contrast. Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual smoking images), I4 (within-participant smoking>neutral contrast), I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [FSL]). Inclusion not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical map reported), and therefore I6 does not rescue inclusion because no whole-brain results (even coordinates/figures) for an unmasked whole-brain task effect are provided. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain task maps, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of hedonic food images versus neutral nonfood objects, and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise p<0.01, cluster-level FDR q<0.05) with statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables. Relevant participant information (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task effects, and is primary empirical fMRI data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study is not an fMRI task activation study. It reports EEG/ERP (LORETA) cue-reactivity and DTI tractography data acquired with a structural/DTI sequence (1.5T), but no task-evoked, whole-brain fMRI BOLD contrasts (drug-cues > control) or voxelwise group-level fMRI maps are presented. Therefore it fails core inclusion criteria I3 (functional MRI study), I4 (within-participant fMRI contrast drug-cues>control), and I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map). The manuscript does report participant info, cue types, scanner field strength and processing software, satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are specifically triggered. Based on these gaps, the study must be excluded from the fMRI cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual drug cues (drug-related vs neutral pictures) in a group of male adolescent stimulant abusers. It includes within-subject contrasts of drug cues > neutral cues and reports group-level whole-brain task activation (main effect thresholded at p < .05 FWE; additional whole-brain exploratory maps reported). Methods report participant age and sex, cue types (cocaine/methamphetamine/heroin images), MRI field strength (1.5T Siemens Avanto mobile scanner), and processing software (SPM12). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) with picture stimuli and matched neutral controls. It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking>control (e.g., S2-T2 BEGIN, S4-T4 END) and performs group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level analyses using SPM5 with results reported in tables/figures and described in the text. Participant information (group sizes, sex counts, age stated as no group differences with Table 1), cue type (smoking/nicotine), MRI scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-task whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos) in human participants. The manuscript reports within-subject contrasts of smoking vs. non-smoking cues (smoke>non-smoke), performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL/FLAME1) with cluster-corrected thresholding, and provides behavioral and imaging results. Participant age and sex are reported. Processing software (FSL) and scanner field strength (3T) are stated. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subjects food>nonfood contrast. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (drink x cue interaction maps, with cluster correction) and describes results in text and figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual smoking stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA, post hoc tests, whole-brain regressions) are presented with FDR correction; results are reported in tables/figures with coordinates. Participant demographics (male-only, ages matched), cue type (nicotine/smoking), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8, FSL) are provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3–I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task effect, is empirical fMRI data).

This is a human fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) with within-subject contrasts of food > non-food stimuli. The study performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2, random-effects, whole-brain thresholds) and reports coordinates in tables/figures. Participant sex is reported (2 male, 4 female), cue type is food, MRI field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM2) are described. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study).

This paper reports an fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual/manipulated cues (participants held and viewed a cigarette via live video feed). The authors present within-subject contrasts (cigarette cue > control cue) and report a main effect of cue with whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level analyses (GLM and mixed-model ANOVA) and cluster-corrected maps. Results are presented as tables of coordinates and figures, and methods report participant ages/sex distribution, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Allegra), and processing software (AFNI, FSL, etc.). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task activation, empirical human fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in daily smokers. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing smoking-cue versus control/neutral delay conditions and presents voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (GLM, random-effects ANOVA) with cluster-correction and figures/tables of results. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

EXCLUSION (E3) applied: The study reports predominantly ROI- and system-based analyses (VS/OFC spherical ROIs and aggregated network ROIs) and does not present or report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or peak coordinates from whole-brain task analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of food cues > control images was computed). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), and therefore I6 cannot be applied. I7 (reporting of participant age) is incompletely reported (sample described as undergraduates; no mean/age range given), so I7 is not satisfied. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion; however absence of whole-brain task results leads to exclusion under E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood images, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps (two-sample t tests and flexible factorial analyses) with results presented in figures and tables, and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues with a within-subject contrast (food > control) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results with coordinates; participant age/sex and scanner field strength (3 T) are reported. However, the provided full text does not specify the fMRI processing software (e.g., SPM, FSL, AFNI) in the main methods (it may appear in Supplementary Information, but that was not provided). Therefore inclusion criterion I7 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Based on the requirement that all inclusion criteria must be met, I exclude this study.

This study is not an fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual stimuli. It is a behavioral/clinical factor analysis of alcohol use disorder using questionnaires, neuropsychological tests, and MIMIC/ROC analyses; no fMRI methods, task contrasts, whole-brain activation maps, or MRI acquisition/processing details are reported. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a functional MRI study assessing cue-reactivity with visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control or reward-cue>control contrast), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I6 (no whole-brain results reported in any form), I7 (MRI-related details and cue-type as fMRI stimuli not provided). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply (study is empirical but non-fMRI). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (high-calorie food images) with a within-participant contrast (high-calorie food > brick wall control). A group-level, whole-brain voxelwise 2nd-level analysis (SPM5) is reported with cluster and voxel statistics and figures/tables describing results. Participant ages and sex (30M, 39F, 44F), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports a within-participant contrast of appetizing > bland foods and conducts group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses using SPM5 with reported peak coordinates and statistical maps; participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only without task activation; not between-group-only; not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material not required. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria.

This study meets inclusion for fMRI visual cue-reactivity to a natural reward (food). It reports within-subject contrasts of high-calorie food cues > control objects and includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (exploratory voxelwise analyses with cluster correction; Figure 5 and Table 4 report cluster coordinates). Sufficient details on participants (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL, FreeSurfer, ANTs, AFNI) are provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

The provided 'full text' consists only of a website privacy/cookie notice and does not contain core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I cannot verify any inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria I3–I7 cannot be confirmed: (I3) whether this is a functional MRI study of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli is not verifiable; (I4) whether there is a within-participant contrast (cues>control) is not reported; (I5/I6) whether any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps or coordinate tables are reported is unknown; (I7) participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software are not present. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be determined from the provided content. Because the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

Full text is a complete empirical fMRI study that examines favorite-food (natural reward), stress, and neutral cues, reports participant ages/sex, scanner (3T), and processing software, and presents whole-brain, voxelwise, FWE-corrected group results and within-subject contrasts. However, the cue modality is personalized guided-imagery presented auditorily (audio scripts), not visual stimuli. The meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). Therefore study fails inclusion criterion I3 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is an fMRI study of natural (sexual) reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (erotic images). The task modeled cue and reward phases with within-subject contrasts (e.g., erotic-cue vs control) and reported group-level results. The manuscript explicitly states a whole-brain second-level contrast is presented in Supplementary Figure S3 (qualifying whole-brain results reported in supplement), and provides participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength (3T), and processing/toolbox information (MarsBaR, WFU PickAtlas, MATLAB). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary figures are referenced (acceptable per inclusion I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting) are met because whole-brain results are reported. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward: food cues using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrast high-calorie food > nonfood), and I7 (reported participant age/sex, cue type: food, scanner field strength: 3T, processing software: SPM5). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map reported; analysis was voxelwise but restricted to a predefined anatomical mask/ROIs). Exclusion criterion met: E3 (reports voxelwise results only within preselected ROI/mask and corrects within those regions; no whole-brain results presented). Therefore the study is excluded for lacking whole-brain task activation results required by the review.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in treatment-seeking smokers. It reports within-subject contrasts comparing smoking vs neutral images (LookSmoking > LookNeutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with cluster-wise correction; results are presented in tables/figures. Methods report scanner field strength (Siemens Allegra 3.0T), processing software (SPM8; AlphaSim in AFNI for correction), and participant characteristics (adult smokers abstinent 12 h; sex was recorded and analyzed; demographic table referenced). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (highly palatable vs. neutral and vs. moderate) and reports group-level whole-brain analyses (whole-brain results referenced in Supporting Information, including a figure showing activation). Participant demographics (female, age 18–25) and cue type are reported; MRI acquisition and processing details are noted as provided in the Supporting Information (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study in smokers using visual stimuli related to smoking (graphic warning labels). It reports within-subject contrasts (LABEL>CONTROL and HIGH>LOW) comparing smoking-related images to scrambled control images, conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction, and provides tables/figures of peak coordinates. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine/graphic cigarette warnings), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual methamphetamine-related images in treatment-seeking MA users. It includes within-participant contrasts of MA cues > neutral cues, and presents group-level whole-brain, voxel-wise task activation analyses using FSL, BROCCOLI, and RANDOMISE with permutation testing (figures and cluster-corrected maps reported). Relevant details are provided: cue type (methamphetamine), MRI scanner field strength (3-T Siemens Prisma), processing software (FSL, BROCCOLI, RANDOMISE), and participant demographics are reported (see Table 1 and text). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only unmasked contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the article meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an ASL perfusion fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual/audiovisual smoking vs non-smoking stimuli with within-subject SC>non-SC contrasts, and participant/scanner/processing details are reported. However, all neuroimaging analyses are reported as ROI-based (using a Harvard–Oxford ROI mask) and the paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported) and fails to meet the required whole-brain analysis inclusion criterion (I5). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI drug cue reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrast SCs>control), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, processing software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map). Note: coordinates and ROI cluster results are reported in tables/figures, but these derive from ROI-masked analyses rather than an unmasked whole-brain voxelwise map, so I6 does not rescue the study for whole-brain requirement.

This is an empirical task fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (24 heroin-related vs 24 neutral images). The study reports a within-participant contrast (heroin-related > neutral) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and post-hoc contrasts) with whole-brain multiple-comparison correction (Monte Carlo simulation via AFNI). Results are reported in figures and tables of coordinates. Participant characteristics (male-only sample, group sizes, demographics referenced in Table 1), cue type (heroin), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (DPARSF, SPM8, AFNI) are all reported. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. All required inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine-related visual stimuli (FDA graphic warning labels) measuring cue-reactivity and craving. It includes within-subject contrasts of graphic (drug-related) > non-graphic (control) labels and reports group-level voxelwise activation results (clustered coordinates and thresholding) and voxelwise PPI connectivity results. The paper provides participant age/sex details, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (colored/positioned squares) that predict monetary gains, losses, or neutral outcomes, providing cue-reactivity to a secondary (non-drug) reward. The GLMs modeled anticipation and outcome events (gain, loss, neutral/bivalent), enabling within-participant contrasts of reward-related cues versus neutral/baseline (e.g., gain anticipation/outcome > neutral). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables of significant clusters (Tables 5 and 6) and voxelwise interaction results, satisfying whole-brain map requirements. Relevant metadata are reported (participant age/sex details, cue type: monetary visual stimuli, MRI field strength: 3T, processing software: AFNI and FSL). No exclusion criteria are met: the study includes whole-brain task activation maps (not ROI-only), is not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and provides within-subject task contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual natural-reward cues (food and sexual images) and reports both ROI and whole-brain group-level task analyses. Inclusion criteria met: (I3) fMRI cue-reactivity to natural rewards using visual stimuli (food, sexual); (I4) within-participant contrasts of natural reward cues > baseline/control (food > baseline; sexual scenes > baseline) were computed; (I5) group-level, whole-brain (second-level random-effects) statistical images were created and reported; (I6) whole-brain results are described in the text with stereotactic coordinates and region names; (I7) participant age and sex (female, 18–19), cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This article is a narrative/review piece summarizing neuroimaging research on cigarette craving and self-control and does not present original human fMRI data or methods/results. The provided full text contains only abstract/metadata and lacks empirical methods, participants, within-participant contrasts, or whole-brain voxelwise activation maps. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data). No inclusion criteria are met: I3 (functional MRI cue-reactivity with visual stimuli) not met; I4 (within-participant contrast cues>control) not met; I5/I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported) not met; I7 (reporting participant age/sex, cue type, scanner strength, processing software) not met. Full text appears incomplete for screening and contains no original data or results, so fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) visual cues and uses within-subject contrasts (fattening > non-fattening), and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). However, the paper presents results as region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (mean ROI z-scores in five a priori ROIs) and does not report any group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps, coordinate tables, or unmasked whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual natural reward (erotic) cue-reactivity. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports within-subject contrasts of erotic cue > control (and monetary cue > control) at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM2 analyses with cluster-level correction and coordinates/figures. Participant demographics (age, all heterosexual males) and scanner details (1.5 T Siemens Sonata) and preprocessing/software (SPM2) are provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol using taste (alcohol vs. juice) in 300 participants with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and reported demographics/scanner/processing details. It meets I4 (within-participant alcohol>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described), and I7 (reports age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, processing software). However, it fails I3 because the cue modality is gustatory (taste), not visual stimuli required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual sexual cues (a natural reward) in Parkinson’s patients. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (sexual vs neutral and sexual vs other rewards) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholds and cluster correction reported; whole-brain results presented in figures and supplementary tables). Methods include participant age/sex info, cue type (sexual), MRI field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM5). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes unmasked task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using visual drug cues (nicotine/smoking) with both smokers and non-smokers, including age/sex information. Within-subject contrasts of smoking versus matched control stimuli are computed (BEGIN/ID, END/ID, BEGIN/DIS, END/DIS). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FLAME in FSL) with thresholded Z statistic images and results reported in tables/figures. Scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are specified. The article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural reward–related (sexual) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of sexual versus control stimuli (sexual condition minus neutral and emotional controls), and performs group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses (second-level random effects) with tabulated MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. Relevant methodological details required by the review are present: participant sex and age-inclusion criteria, cue type (sexual), MRI field strength (3-T), and processing software (SPM12). Results are reported as whole-brain activations in figures/tables/supplement. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task maps, and is an original empirical fMRI study). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion based on E3: the paper reports only ROI-constrained task results rather than an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrasts of food cues > fixation/control were performed), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no evidence of a group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map presented; reported results are ROI-based). Full text appears complete. Because the review requires whole-brain task maps (or reported coordinates/figures from whole-brain analyses), this study must be excluded under E3.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) across ages. It reports within-subject task contrasts of food stimuli versus baseline (Far+Close > fixation/baseline), which qualifies as a cues>control contrast. Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise results are reported (tables/figures) and processing details (SPM8), scanner field strength (3T), participant age and sex, and cue type (food) are provided. Although no separate neutral image control was used, the reported food>baseline contrast meets the review's requirement for a within-participant cue>control analysis. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using erotic (sexual) visual cues in Parkinson’s patients and healthy controls; it meets I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual sexual stimuli). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task analyses with tables of coordinates and figures (SPM8 was used), satisfying I5 and I6. However, it does not present a within-participant contrast of reward-cues > control stimuli (no simple erotic cue > neutral/control image contrast is reported; analyses focus on parametric modulation of subjective value and delay-related contrasts), so I4 is not met. Also, the provided full text does not report MRI scanner field strength (e.g., 1.5T/3T) in the methods excerpt, so the required reporting elements in I7 are incomplete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria (specifically I4 and I7) and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with a within-subject contrast (Food > Activities). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (thresholds and clusters reported; tables/figures described) and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.
