This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (Coke product and logo advertisements). It includes within-participant contrasts of reward cues > control (Coke product ads > non-food ads; Coke logo ads > non-food ads; all Coke ads > non-food ads). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, with appropriate cluster-wise FWE correction and results reported in tables/figures. Relevant methodological details are reported: participant sample (27 adolescents), cue type (food/soft drink), scanner field strength (Siemens Allegra 3T), and processing software (SPM8, AFNI). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains unmasked whole-brain task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food stimuli (natural reward) in children, with within-participant contrasts (high- and low-calorie blocks, blurred images used as baseline) and a group-level whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA. The paper reports whole-brain clusters (Table 1, figures), scanner field strength (3.0T), participant ages/sex, cue type (food), and processing software (AFNI). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking and neutral pictures). The design includes within-participant contrasts (craving vs neutral and regulation vs craving) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise results (SPM8) with cluster correction and coordinate peaks. Relevant study descriptors are reported: participant age and sex (right-handed males, mean age 41.3), cue type (nicotine/smoking cues), scanner field strength (Siemens Verio 3T) and processing software (SPM8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (complete). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without whole-brain task effects, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (milkshake vs tasteless solution). It includes within-participant contrasts of unpaired milkshake cue > unpaired tasteless cue, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with thresholding and small-volume corrections, and provides coordinate tables/figures. Participant age/sex (young adult females), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

The provided "full text" is only a website privacy/cookie notice and does not contain the article’s introduction, methods, results, or discussion. Therefore the full text is incomplete and core information cannot be verified. I cannot confirm that this is an fMRI study using visual reward cues (I3), that it contains a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control (I4), that it reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps (I5/I6), or that it reports necessary participant and scanning details (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met based on the available content, but because the full text is missing I cannot apply inclusion criteria. Recommend obtaining the complete article PDF or full text for reassessment.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). It reports within-subject contrasts of high-calorie > low-calorie and high-calorie > neutral stimuli, and presents whole-brain, voxelwise SPM results (maps, tables of clusters and MNI/Talairach coordinates). Methods report scanner field strength (3 T), processing software (SPM5), cue type (food), and participant sex (two women, one man; described as three adults). Core sections (methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria for visual-cue fMRI activation analyses are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study using food (natural) rewards with visual fractal cues predicting food outcomes, meeting cue-reactivity requirements. The paper reports within-participant cue contrasts (reward-predicting cue vs. reward-omission cue) at the cue phase, satisfying a cues>control-type contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-threshold corrected maps and tables/figures), and whole-brain results are described in the text. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Allegra), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are provided. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject whole-brain task effects). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with within-participant contrasts of food > nonfood control stimuli. Group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) activation maps are reported (figures and Supplemental Table 2) with cluster correction; ROI analyses are also reported but do not replace whole-brain results. Necessary study descriptors are provided (participant age and sex, cue type: food, scanner: 3T Siemens, processing software: BrainVoyager). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food pictures) and includes within-subject contrasts (food > neutral and food > pleasant). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM5; coordinates/tables and figures provided). The manuscript reports participant age and sex, cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task activation maps, and is empirical). Full article text with methods, results, and discussion is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a study protocol (planned longitudinal fMRI trial) without reported empirical fMRI results or task-evoked whole-brain statistical maps. Exclusion met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data). Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI study of a natural reward—food—using visual stimuli), I4 (planned within-participant contrasts of food cues vs control stimuli are described). Inclusion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported in the paper), I7 (processing/software for fMRI preprocessing/analysis not clearly specified). Although whole-brain analyses are planned, the manuscript contains no empirical results/maps to meet the meta-analysis requirements. Full text appears to be a complete protocol but lacks results, so fulltext_incomplete=true for the purposes of data extraction.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food images (natural reward cues); it reports within-subject contrasts of craved>neutral foods (LC>LN and LC>LNC) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM8 with AlphaSim correction, with clusters described in the text. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0T Siemens Allegra), and processing software are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study is an fMRI investigation of visual food cues (natural reward) and meets I3 (fMRI of natural reward-related visual cues), I4 (within-participant contrast: fattening vs. non-fattening/control stimuli), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type: food, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software: FSL/AFNI/FreeSurfer). However, the full text reports an ROI-based analysis approach (functionally-defined ROIs combined with the Harvard-Oxford atlas) and presents results averaged across ROIs; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain results are described. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Conclusion: EXCLUDED (E3).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food vs neutral images) in humans. It includes within-participant contrasts of food>neutral (food–neutral image contrast) and reports group-level task-evoked results. Although some ROI analyses were used, the paper also reports whole-brain multivariate (task and non-rotated PLS) analyses with reported clusters and bootstrap ratios (clusters reported with peak and voxel extent), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps (coordinate/cluster reporting acceptable per I6). Participant age and sex (female, 18–40), cue type (food), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM5, PLS code) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of methamphetamine-paired versus placebo-paired cues using compound visual-auditory stimuli (visual component present). It reports within-subject contrasts comparing drug-paired > placebo-paired cues and conducts group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (AFNI 3dmvm; cluster-corrected results reported in text, table and figure). Relevant participant info (age range, N, sex used as covariate), cue type (methamphetamine), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (AFNI) are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical human fMRI data present). Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are provided, so fulltext appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using visual cues (chocolate picture; mouldy drink) to probe natural reward-related cue-reactivity and reporting within-participant contrasts of cue>control (pleasant/unpleasant cue vs grey image). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM8; whole-brain cluster- and FWE-corrected results and stereotactic coordinates in tables/figures). Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of appetitive (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual sexual (erotic) stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of CS+ > CS− (natural reward-related cues > control) at the group level, including whole-brain group analyses with reported voxel-wise results and MNI coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual fractal cues predicting a natural reward (juice) and neutral/aversive liquids, meeting the review’s focus on natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-participant analyses of cue-related responses: model-based parametric regressors at cue onsets (expected value / RPE) that effectively contrast reward-predicting vs neutral cues. Group-level voxelwise (second-level) statistical maps are reported with peak coordinates (ventral striatum, SN, amygdala), satisfying the requirement for group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results. Coordinates and cluster information are provided in the text. Participant age and sex, cue type (juice, aversive liquid), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8, FSL) are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

The full text is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (infant faces) in mothers with substance addictions. It includes within-subject contrasts (own-happy vs unknown-happy; own-sad vs unknown-sad), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and cluster tables/figures, and provides necessary methodological details (participant ages/sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, BrainVoyager processing). All required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study examines visual food cue-reactivity (I3) and includes a within-participant contrast of food>control stimuli (I4). Participant demographics, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported (I7). However, the paper reports ROI-based results for the cue-reactivity contrast (NAcc ROI) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical map for the cue-reactivity contrast in the full text. Although a whole-brain peak/ROI for the go/no-go (IFG) is reported, that is not the cue-reactivity contrast of interest. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and is excluded under E3 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain cue-reactivity results).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in children. The design used within-subject block regressors including food image conditions and non-food control conditions and tested within-participant contrasts (e.g., High-ED vs Low-ED; portion-size contrasts; and the GLM included control regressors), reported whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with cluster correction and peak coordinates (Table 3), and provided relevant participant demographics, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (BRAINVOYAGER). Results include whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates. No exclusion criteria were met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity of natural rewards and provides suitable whole-brain data.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). The study reports within-participant contrasts (food > nonfood and high-calorie > nonfood) and used group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrast images entered into ANOVAs and whole-brain exploration with results reported and peak coordinates in Table 1). Results are reported in the text, figures, and tables with MNI coordinates and small-volume FWE correction; scanner field strength (3.0 T), processing software (SPM8), and participant demographics (age range 40–65, all female, N=10) are specified. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, figures, and references) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3. Although it is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol and contains a within-participant contrast (Alcohol Taste > Water Taste) and whole-brain, voxelwise results, the cue modality is gustatory (oral alcohol tastes) rather than visual images/videos. The visual component was limited to brief text labels indicating trial type and does not constitute the required visual cue presentation for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant drug cue > control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, 3.0T scanner field strength, and processing software FSL reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (use of visual stimuli). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). Full text appears complete and sufficient for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study does not report a task-based, within-participant fMRI cue-reactivity contrast (e.g., food cues > control stimuli). Although it used visual food images for behavioral ratings outside the scanner and performed whole-brain voxelwise analyses of resting CBF changes (insulin vs placebo), there is no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map of visual cue-reactivity. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant age/sex, cue type: food, scanner field strength, and processing software are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (functional MRI assessing visual cue-reactivity), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain cue-reactivity results to accept in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore this study is ineligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (chocolate) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (chocolate vs neutral pictures). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (chocolate>neutral), performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (F-maps with cluster correction) and presents resulting fROIs with Talairach coordinates in tables/figures. Relevant participant and methodology details are reported (female participants, age group description, cue type: food/chocolate, 3-T MRI scanner, BrainVoyager processing). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The within-subject contrasts include sexual>neutral at both supraliminal and subliminal levels. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM5; uncorrected and FWE-corrected results; tables/figures described). Participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues (I3 not met). It also lacks a within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control (I4 not met). The paper does satisfy several other criteria: it reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (I5), reports peak coordinates/figures (I6), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (monetary), MRI field strength (3T across sites), and processing software (SPM8) (I7). None of the exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an fMRI investigation of resting cerebral blood flow 4 h after ingestion of high- vs low-GI meals (food intake manipulation), not a cue-reactivity task using visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not assess drug/natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (no within-participant contrast of cues > control stimuli). Although the study reports whole-brain voxelwise comparisons between meal conditions and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) (I7 satisfied), it does not contain task-evoked visual cue contrasts required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore exclude.

This article is a narrative review of neuroimaging studies of the orbitofrontal cortex in substance abuse and does not present original empirical human fMRI task data. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an empirical fMRI study assessing cue-reactivity with visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cues > control contrast reported as original analyses), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps from original fMRI data), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results from the article itself), I7 (the paper summarizes other studies but does not itself report the required participant-level details/scanner field strength/processing software for an original fMRI dataset). Full text appears complete (review article). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study used a monetary incentive delay task (monetary cues) rather than drug cues or the natural reward types of interest (e.g., food, sexual) specified by the review, so it does not meet I3. Although the study includes within-participant contrasts of reward cues versus neutral (gain>neutral, loss>neutral) (I4), reports group-level coordinates and tables (I6), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM5) (I7), it did not acquire whole-brain coverage (authors state whole-brain images were not acquired) and primary analyses used a ventral striatum ROI with small-volume correction. Therefore it fails the requirement for a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map (I5) and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting/no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion); fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study does not meet the review’s focus on cue-reactivity to drug or specified natural reward cues. Although the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (gain/loss anticipation contrasts) and presents results in figures/tables (satisfying I5 and I6), it does not investigate drug-related or the specified natural reward cues (nicotine, alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, heroin, food, or sexual) — instead it uses monetary (secondary) reward cues (MID task). It also does not include a within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control or natural reward-cues > control as required (I4). Information required by I7 (explicit reporting of cue type as one of the review’s target cue categories and clear participant sex reporting in the available text) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded.

Excluded because study reports only a hypothalamic ROI analysis and does not present a group-level, whole-brain task activation map or any within-subject cue>control visual cue-reactivity contrasts. Exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only without whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant age/sex, cue type = food, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (fMRI assessing cue-reactivity using visual stimuli — fMRI measured response to oral glucose, not to presented visual cues), I4 (no within-participant cues>control contrast reported), I5/I6 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group results reported or described). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI experiment of monetary (natural) reward cue processing using visual cues and reports within-participant contrasts of reward vs neutral (gain-neutral) and provides participant demographics, scanner (3T) and processing software (AFNI) — meeting I3, I4, and I7. However, although voxel-wise analyses and cluster-correction methods are described, the manuscript focuses on region-of-interest (small-volume-corrected) results within predefined MCL ROIs and does not present or describe an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map suitable for inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/SVC-reported results with no whole-brain map). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given the lack of an unmasked whole-brain task activation map, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using the monetary incentive delay (MID) task with visual cues (geometric cues signaling monetary gain/loss). It reports within-participant contrasts of gain anticipation versus no-reward (e.g., +¥20/+¥100/+¥500 > ¥0). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described and thresholding (voxel p<0.001, cluster-level FWE p<0.05) is reported; NAc ROI and whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures. Relevant participant information (n=19; 9 males, 10 females; demographics in Table 1), MRI scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (drug-related) and control stimuli with within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral and other category contrasts). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (random-effects ANOVA) with cluster-level correction; results are reported with Talairach coordinates and figures/tables. Key methodological details required by I7 are reported: participant demographics (group sizes and age comparisons; Table 1 indicated), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (Philips 3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only without task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study is a resting-state fMRI pharmacological crossover study of acute naltrexone effects on functional connectivity; it does not present any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural reward cues, nor any within-participant task contrast of cue>control. Therefore it does not meet the review’s inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity tasks and whole-brain task-evoked maps. Exclusion ID met: E4 (study reports only resting-state/connectivity analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (not a task-based cue-reactivity fMRI study using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant cue>control task contrast), I5 (no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map), I6 (not applicable because there are no task whole-brain results to report), I7 (cue type not applicable/reported as a cue paradigm). Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it reports resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses (insula connectivity) rather than a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only seed-based/resting-state connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports relevant participant demographics and scanner/processing details: age range and sex breakdown, cue type = food, 3.0-T scanner field strength, and processing software SPM8/MATLAB). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a task-based fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli during scanning), I4 (no within-participant task contrast of cues > control stimuli), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported), I6 (not applicable because no task-based whole-brain results are provided). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the paper does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for task-evoked cue-reactivity contrasts and is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (beer) cue-reactivity using visual predictive cues (abstract shapes) and within-subject beer>water contrasts. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholding described) and provides coordinates/figures and NeuroVault maps. Participant age/sex (males 18–25), cue type (alcohol/beer), MRI scanner (3T PRISMA) and processing software (SPM8, FSL ICA-AROMA) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E6 applies: the article is a narrative review (no original human fMRI data) and the provided full text is only an abstract and references. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no original functional MRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli reported), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control contrasts), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps), I6 (no clearly described whole-brain results), I7 (no participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, or processing software reported). Full text is incomplete (only abstract/references).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue-reactivity stimuli (alcohol, marijuana, polydrugs, appetitive images) and reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol>neutral, marijuana>neutral, polydrug>neutral, appetitive>neutral). Methods describe group-level, mixed-effects (whole-brain/voxelwise) analyses and thresholding for the cue reactivity task, and results include neural responses (NAcc) to these cue contrasts. Participant demographics, cue types, scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (FSL v5.0) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol advertisements as cues and reports within-subject ALCOHOL > CONTROL contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are reported with cluster correction and peak coordinates (ALCOHOL > CONTROL), presented in tables/figures. Methods report participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3.0T Philips Achieva), and processing software (SPM8). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual nicotine-related (e-cigarette) advertising stimuli and reports within-participant contrasts of e-cigarette > neutral images. A whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis (e-cigarette vs. neutral) is reported with cluster-based correction; results are presented in tables and figures. The manuscript provides participant age and sex information, cue type (nicotine/e-cigarette), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity studies (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of food versus non-food pictures, and reports group-level voxelwise second-level analyses (with results reported via ROI small-volume correction and cluster/voxelwise thresholds). Methods report scanner field strength (3.0T), processing software (SPM8), participant age range and sex matching, and cue type (food). Results are presented as whole-brain task-evoked maps/coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., appetizing foods > bland foods; appetizing foods > nonfood objects), conducted group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (whole-brain SPM results reported with coordinates and figures/supplemental tables), and provides participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM99). Results include voxelwise activation maps/coordinates for contrasts of interest. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward (food) cue-reactivity in women with bulimia nervosa. The study includes within-participant contrasts of food>low-level baseline and food>non-food (post-hoc), reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps and between-group whole-brain analyses with coordinates, and provides participant sex, age information (in Table), cue type (food), scanner field strength (1.5T GE Signa) and processing software (XBAM v4.1). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (erotic) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts and detailed reporting of participants (age, sex), cue type (sexual, monetary), scanner (3T) and processing software (SPM) — meeting I3, I4, I6, and I7. However, the imaging results are reported and analyzed using predefined ROIs (sphere-based ROI analyses) and the reported results focus on ROI statistics; no unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps are presented in the main text. Therefore the study does not provide whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps as required by I5 and effectively reports only ROI-based results, triggering exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper includes original fMRI data using visual food cues (natural reward) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI, 3T) with coordinates. Thus it meets I3, I5, I6, and I7. However, the reported fMRI results focus on contrasts of high-ED versus low-ED food images (food vs. food) and do not present a within-participant cue>control (e.g., food>neutral/furniture) contrast result required by I4. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (pictures of candy/dessert) to probe natural reward–related cue reactivity in a within-subject, placebo-controlled design. The authors report within-participant analyses comparing task conditions (food stimulus epochs) relative to a low-level baseline and report whole-brain, voxelwise group results with FWE-corrected clusters and MNI coordinates. Participant age/sex (31 healthy adult females), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (SPM8) are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of analyses. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of smokers using pictorial (visual) drug-related cues (nicotine) and includes a within-subject contrast of smoking cues > neutral cues (LCSP minus LCNP). Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted (random-effects RM-ANOVA and between-group t-tests) and results are reported with coordinates and figures; ROI small-volume corrections were applied but whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses were performed and reported. Relevant methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner, SPM8 processing). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward stimuli (food images) with a within-participant contrast of food > nonfood. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain contrast maps, cluster correction) and also provides ROI analyses; whole-brain results are described in the text and supplemental materials. Participant age and sex (22F/17M, age range 25–70), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager, SPSS) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7).

The study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol (drug) cue processing using visual stimuli (I3 met). It reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps for respond alcohol > rest and respond neutral > rest (cluster-corrected) (I5 met) and provides necessary reporting (age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner, FSL processing) (I7 met). Whole-brain results are described in text/figures (I6 met). However, the study did NOT perform the required within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., alcohol > neutral); authors explicitly state they did not conduct direct comparisons between respond alcohol and respond neutral conditions because the task was not structured to allow a clean contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met, and the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in humans using visual food cues (natural reward) and assesses cue-reactivity. First-level contrasts include food > nonfood and high-calorie food > nonfood (within-participant contrasts). Data were analyzed at the group level using voxelwise second-level (three-way ANOVA) analyses in SPM8, and results are reported with coordinates/figures (Supplementary Table 1 and brain slices), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps (with small-volume correction applied within a priori ROIs). Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete/unavailable: the provided content is only a redirect/metadata page (no introduction, methods, results, or discussion). Therefore I cannot verify any required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 cannot be confirmed). Exclusion criteria met: none. Rationale: Without the full text I cannot confirm that this is a task-based fMRI study using visual drug or natural reward cues (I3), that it reports within-participant cue>control contrasts (I4), that it provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps or coordinates (I5/I6), or that it reports participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (I7). Per screening rules, fulltext_incomplete takes precedence; study is excluded until full text is available for assessment.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (photographs) of a natural reward (romantic partner) versus a neutral familiar person, with within-participant contrasts (rejecter > neutral). Group-level, voxelwise analyses were performed (mixed-effects GLM) and whole-brain results are reported (thresholded at p<0.001 uncorrected with cluster coordinates/tables). Relevant methodological and participant details are reported (age, sex distribution, cue type description, 1.5 T scanner field strength, and SPM2 processing). Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity to a natural reward using visual stimuli and reports whole-brain task-evoked maps in the text/tables. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food (HCF) versus nonfood (NF) and low-calorie food (LCF) versus NF, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected) with reported coordinates/ROIs. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T Siemens), and processing software (BioImageSuite, AFNI) are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of marzipan objects). It reports within-subject contrasts (CS+ > CS-) at the first level and a group-level one-sample t-test whole-brain voxelwise analysis (exploratory whole-brain results reported at p < .001 uncorrected, with cluster reporting and SVC results). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM12). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria.

This fMRI study directly assesses natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual/abstract food cues in a food incentive delay (FID) task and compares high vs no reward (10 SP vs 0 SP) within participants. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected whole-brain results and supplementary tables of coordinates) as well as ROI analyses. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI results, connectivity-only analyses, or only between-group contrasts; it provides within-subject contrasts and unmasked whole-brain task effects. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary tables/figures are referenced for coordinates. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food pictures) with within-subject contrasts (food pictures versus baseline/control and high vs low caloric food) across conditions (glucose vs water). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM8 (full-factorial ANOVA) and results are reported in tables/figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software are reported. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

Exclusion applied: E6. This paper is a narrative review discussing mechanisms of portion size and summarizes prior studies; it is not an original empirical human fMRI study reporting task-evoked whole-brain results. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not present an original functional MRI study with task activation maps), I4 (no within-participant contrasts of drug or natural reward cues > control reported), I5/I6 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate-based whole-brain results provided), I7 (does not report requisite participant demographics, cue-type fMRI details, scanner field strength, or processing software for an original dataset). The full text appears complete (not truncated). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol stimuli (social and non-social alcohol pictures) in young adult males. Within-participant contrasts comparing alcohol versus soda cues were reported (e.g., (SA+NA)>(SS+NS) and interaction (SA>SS)-(NA>NS)). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded (voxel p<.001, cluster-level FWE p<.05), and unthresholded T-maps are available on NeuroVault. Relevant participant and scanner/processing details are provided (age, sex, cue type: alcohol, 3T Siemens PRISMA(Fit), SPM8, ICA-AROMA). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol vs control taste) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FLAME/FSL), as well as participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). However, the meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). This study used gustatory (taste) cues with accompanying visual instructions rather than visual cue stimuli, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I3. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I3. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of food (HC and LC) versus neutral (NF) images, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2x3 ANOVA, whole-brain FWE correction via AlphaSim) with reported brain regions and contrast maps. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM5, AFNI, BioImageSuite). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. This study used interleaved TMS/BOLD to measure TMS-evoked BOLD responses and applied cTBS; it did not present visual drug or natural reward cues as a task nor report a within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli. Therefore it does not meet the core cue-reactivity requirements for the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps of TMS-evoked responses), I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported), I7 (participant demographics and study details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant drug-cue>control contrast).

This study is excluded because it reports resting-state fMRI (ALFF and seed-based functional connectivity) before and after ingestion of yogurt and does not present a within-participant task-based visual cue-reactivity contrast. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant age/sex, cue type = food, MRI field strength = 3T, and processing software SPM8/DPARSF are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an fMRI cue-reactivity paradigm using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug- or natural reward-cues > control stimuli contrasts), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Full text appears complete. Thus the study does not meet the review’s task-based visual cue-reactivity requirements and is excluded.
